translations.literal: Visiting and sacrificing at imperial tombs and temples; anniversary of death; protocol for receiving death notices from tributary kings; protocol for raising lamentation for princes and great ministers; protocol for attending the funerals of princes and great ministers; protocol for the inner palace mourning for fathers and grandfathers; protocol for dispatching envoys to offer condolences; protocol for dispatching envoys to confer posthumous gifts on princes and great ministers; bestowal of sacrificial offerings and burial; regulations for funerals and burials, steles and tablets; bestowal of posthumous titles and funeral rites for ranked officials; funeral rites for scholars and commoners; mourning garments and periods
translations.idiomatic: Visiting and sacrificing at mausoleums and temples; death anniversaries; receiving obituary memorials from tributary kings; raising lamentation for princes and senior ministers; attending the funerals of princes and senior ministers; inner-palace mourning for paternal ancestors; dispatching envoys to offer condolences; dispatching envoys to confer posthumous enfeoffments on princes and senior ministers; grants for sacrifice and burial; regulations on burial and funeral monuments; posthumous titles and ranked officials' funeral rites; scholar-commoner funeral rites; mourning dress and service periods

sentences.zh: ○謁祭陵廟

translations.literal: ○ Visiting and sacrificing at imperial tombs and temples
translations.idiomatic: ○ On visiting and sacrificing at mausoleums and temples

sentences.zh: 八年，詔翰林院議陵寢朔望節序祭祀禮。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, an edict ordered the Hanlin Academy to deliberate the ritual for sacrifices at the imperial mausoleum on the first and fifteenth of the month and on seasonal festivals.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, the throne ordered the Hanlin Academy to draft ritual for offerings at the imperial mausoleum on new and full moons and at seasonal observances.

sentences.zh: 學士樂韶鳳等言：「漢諸廟寢園有便殿，日祭於寢，月祭於廟，時祭於便殿。

translations.literal: Academician Yue Shaofeng and others said: "The Han had convenient halls in the park-tombs of the various temples; daily sacrifice was in the sleeping chamber, monthly sacrifice in the temple, and seasonal sacrifice in the convenient hall.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin academician Yue Shaofeng and others reported: "Under the Han, each temple park-tomb had a side hall: daily offerings were made in the sleeping chamber, monthly in the main temple, and seasonal in the side hall.

sentences.zh: 後漢都洛陽，以關西諸陵久遠，但四時用特牲祀。

translations.literal: Later Han, having established the capital at Luoyang, because the tombs west of the Pass were far away, used only a special victim for sacrifice in the four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Han moved the capital to Luoyang, the Guanxi tombs lay too distant for regular attendance; only the four seasonal sacrifices with a special victim were kept.

sentences.zh: 每西幸，即親詣。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor went west on tour, he personally visited them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor toured west, he went in person.

sentences.zh: 歲正月祀郊廟畢，以次上洛陽諸陵。

translations.literal: Each year, after the suburban and temple sacrifices of the first month were completed, he proceeded in turn to the tombs at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: After the first month's suburban and ancestral rites were finished, he visited the Luoyang tombs in sequence.

sentences.zh: 唐園陵之制，皇祖以上陵，皆朔望上食，元日、冬至、寒食、伏臘、社各一祭。

translations.literal: Under the Tang system for park-tombs, for tombs of imperial ancestors and above, on the first and fifteenth of each month food was offered; on New Year's Day, the winter solstice, Cold Food, the dog-days and year-end festivals, and the community sacrifice, each had one sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang park-tomb regulations, tombs of the imperial forebears and above received food on every new and full moon, and one sacrifice each on New Year's Day, the winter solstice, Cold Food, the dog-days and year-end festivals, and the community rite.

sentences.zh: 皇考陵，朔望及節祭日進食，又薦新於諸陵。

translations.literal: For the tomb of the imperial father, on the first and fifteenth and on festival days food was presented, and new harvest was also offered at the various tombs.
translations.idiomatic: At the imperial father's tomb, offerings came on new and full moons and festival days; fresh harvest was also presented at the various tombs.

sentences.zh: 永徽二年，定獻陵朔望、冬夏至、伏臘、清明、社等節，皆上食。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yonghui, it was fixed that for Xian Mausoleum, on the first and fifteenth, the winter and summer solstices, the dog-days and year-end festivals, Qingming, and the community sacrifice, food was always offered.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghui year 2, Xian Mausoleum was scheduled for food offerings on new and full moons, both solstices, the dog-days and year-end festivals, Qingming, and the community rite.

sentences.zh: 開元中，敕獻、昭、乾、定、橋、恭六陵，朔望上食，冬至、寒食各設一祭。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan period, an imperial order fixed that the six tombs Xian, Zhao, Qian, Ding, Qiao, and Gong received food on the first and fifteenth, and one sacrifice each on the winter solstice and Cold Food.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaiyuan, an edict fixed new- and full-moon offerings and one sacrifice each on the winter solstice and Cold Food for the six tombs: Xian, Zhao, Qian, Ding, Qiao, and Gong.

sentences.zh: 宋每歲春秋仲月，遣太常宗正卿朝諸陵。

translations.literal: The Song each year in the second months of spring and autumn dispatched the Director of the Imperial Sacrifices and the Director of the Imperial Clan to attend the various tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Each year in the second months of spring and autumn, the Song dispatched the Director of Imperial Sacrifices and the Director of the Imperial Clan to attend the tombs.

sentences.zh: 我朝舊儀，每歲元旦、清明、七月望、十月朔、冬至日，俱用太牢，遣官致祭。

translations.literal: Our dynasty's former ritual: each year on New Year's Day, Qingming, the fifteenth of the seventh month, the first of the tenth month, and the winter solstice, all used the great victim and dispatched officials to perform sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Our former practice: on New Year's Day, Qingming, the fifteenth of the seventh month, the first of the tenth month, and the winter solstice, the great victim was used and officials were sent to sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 白塔二處，則用少牢，中官行禮，今擬如舊儀，增夏至日用太牢，其伏臘、社、每月朔望，則用特羊，祠祭署官行禮。

translations.literal: At the two White Pagoda sites, the lesser victim was used and eunuchs performed the rite; now it is proposed to follow the former ritual, adding the summer solstice with the great victim; for the dog-days and year-end festivals, the community sacrifice, and each month's first and fifteenth, a special sheep is used and officials of the Sacrificial Office perform the rite.
translations.idiomatic: At the two White Pagoda sites the lesser victim was offered by eunuchs. It is now proposed to keep the old schedule, add the summer solstice with the great victim, and on the dog-days, year-end festivals, community rite, and each new and full moon use a special sheep, with Sacrificial Office officials performing the rite.

sentences.zh: 如節與朔望、伏臘、社同日，則用節禮。

translations.literal: If a festival day coincides with the first or fifteenth, the dog-days and year-end festivals, or the community sacrifice, the festival ritual is used.
translations.idiomatic: When a festival day falls on the same date as a new or full moon or the dog-days, year-end, or community observances, the festival ritual takes precedence.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The proposal was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: " The court approved.

sentences.zh: 十六年，孝陵殿成，命皇太子以牲醴致祭。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, when the hall of Xiaoling Mausoleum was completed, the heir apparent was ordered to offer sacrifice with victims and libations.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16, when Xiaoling's ritual hall was finished, the heir apparent was commanded to sacrifice with victims and libations.

sentences.zh: 清晨陳祭儀畢，皇太子、親王由東門入，就殿中拜位，皆四拜。

translations.literal: After the morning offerings were set out and the ritual completed, the heir apparent and princes entered by the east gate, took their bowing positions in the hall, and all performed four prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: When the dawn rites were arranged, the heir apparent and princes entered the east gate, took their places in the hall, and each bowed four times.

sentences.zh: 皇太子少前，三上香，奠酒，讀祝曰：「園陵始營，祭享之儀未具。

translations.literal: The heir apparent stepped slightly forward, thrice offered incense, poured libation, and read the prayer: "The park-tomb was first laid out, and the ritual of sacrifice and offering was not yet complete.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent advanced slightly, offered incense three times, poured wine, and read the prayer: "The mausoleum park was newly laid out and sacrificial rites were not yet in place.

sentences.zh: 今禮殿既成，奉安神位，謹用祭告。

translations.literal: Now that the ritual hall is complete and the spirit tablet has been installed, we respectfully use this offering to announce it.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the ritual hall stands complete and the spirit seat is enshrined, we respectfully announce it with this offering.

sentences.zh: 」遂行亞獻、終獻禮，皇太子以下皆四拜，執事行禮皆內官。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the secondary and final offerings were performed; the heir apparent and those below all performed four prostrations; those conducting the rite were all inner-palace eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: " The secondary and final offerings followed; the heir apparent and all below bowed four times; eunuchs of the inner palace conducted the rite.

sentences.zh: 二十六年令，車馬過陵，及守陵官民入陵者，百步外下馬，違者以大不敬論。

translations.literal: An order of the twenty-sixth year: when carriages and horses passed the mausoleum, and officials and people guarding or entering the mausoleum, they dismounted a hundred paces outside; violators were punished as for great irreverence.
translations.idiomatic: In year 26 it was ordered: anyone passing the mausoleum by carriage or on horseback, and any guard or visitor entering it, must dismount a hundred paces away; violation was punished as gross irreverence.

sentences.zh: 建文初，定孝陵每歲正旦、孟冬、忌辰、聖節，俱行香，清明、中元、冬至，俱祭祀。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianwen reign, it was fixed that for Xiaoling each year on New Year's Day, mid-winter, the death anniversary, and the emperor's birthday, incense was offered; on Qingming, the mid-year ghost festival, and the winter solstice, full sacrifice was performed.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianwen, Xiaoling was scheduled for incense on New Year's Day, mid-winter, the death anniversary, and the emperor's birthday, and full sacrifice on Qingming, the mid-year ghost festival, and the winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 勳舊大臣行禮，文武官陪祀。

translations.literal: Meritorious old ministers performed the rite; civil and military officials attended as assistants.
translations.idiomatic: Meritorious elder ministers led the rite; civil and military officials assisted.

sentences.zh: 若親王之籓，過京師者謁陵。

translations.literal: If a prince went to his fief and passed the capital, he visited the mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Princes en route to their fiefs who passed the capital visited the mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 官員以公事至，入城者謁陵，出城者辭陵。

translations.literal: Officials who came on public business bowed at the mausoleum on entering the city and took leave at the mausoleum on leaving.
translations.idiomatic: Officials arriving on state business paid respects at the mausoleum on entering the city and on departure when leaving.

sentences.zh: 國有大事，遣官祭告。

translations.literal: When the state had a great affair, officials were dispatched to announce it in sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: On great affairs of state, envoys were sent to report them in sacrificial announcement.

sentences.zh: 懿文太子陵在孝陵左，四孟、清明、中元、冬至、歲暮及忌辰，凡九祭。

translations.literal: The mausoleum of the heir apparent Yiwen was to the left of Xiaoling; in the four second months, Qingming, the mid-year festival, the winter solstice, year-end, and the death anniversary—in all nine sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Heir apparent Yiwen's tomb lay left of Xiaoling; nine sacrifices were held in the four second months, at Qingming, the mid-year festival, the winter solstice, year-end, and on his death anniversary.

sentences.zh: 弘治元年，遣內官監護鳳陽皇陵，凡官員以公事經過者俱謁陵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongzhi, eunuchs of the Directorate of Palace Eunuchs were sent to guard the imperial mausoleum at Fengyang; all officials passing on public business were to visit the mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi year 1, eunuchs of the Directorate were sent to guard Fengyang's imperial mausoleum; every official passing on public business had to visit it.

sentences.zh: 十七年，更裕陵神座。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, the spirit seats at Yuling were renewed.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 the spirit seats at Yuling were replaced.

sentences.zh: 初，議以孝肅太皇太后祔葬裕陵，已遣官分告諸陵及天壽山后土，而欽天監以爲歲殺在北，方向不利。

translations.literal: At first it was debated to bury Empress Dowager Xiaosu at Yuling in joint burial; officials had already been sent to announce separately at the various mausoleums and at the Queen of Earth on Tianshou Mountain, but the Directorate of Astronomy held that the year's killing qi was in the north and the direction was unfavorable.
translations.idiomatic: At first it was proposed to bury Empress Dowager Xiaosu at Yuling; envoys had announced at every mausoleum and at Tianshou Mountain's Queen of Earth altar, but the Astronomical Directorate said the year's killing force lay north and the direction was ill-omened.

sentences.zh: 內官監亦謂英廟陵寢，難以輕動，遂議別建廟，奉安神主。

translations.literal: The Directorate of Palace Eunuchs also said that moving Yingzong's mausoleum chamber would be difficult; they then debated building a separate temple and installing the spirit tablet there.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch directorate also argued that Yingzong's tomb chamber could not lightly be disturbed; they then proposed a separate temple to enshrine the tablet.

sentences.zh: 帝心未慊，卒移英廟居中，孝莊居左，孝肅祔其右云。

translations.literal: The emperor was not satisfied; in the end Yingzong was moved to the center, Xiaozhuang to the left, and Xiaosu was placed to his right.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was not content; in the end Yingzong was centered, Xiaozhuang placed to his left, and Xiaosu to his right.

sentences.zh: 正德間，定長陵以下諸陵，各設神宮監並衛及祠祭署。

translations.literal: During the Zhengde period, below Changling and the other mausoleums, each was given a Spirit Palace Directorate, guards, and a Sacrificial Office.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhengde, each mausoleum from Changling downward received a Spirit Palace Directorate, guards, and a Sacrificial Office.

sentences.zh: 凡清明、中元、冬至，俱分遣駙馬都尉行禮，文武官陪祭。

translations.literal: On Qingming, the mid-year festival, and the winter solstice, sons-in-law of the emperor were each dispatched to perform the rite; civil and military officials assisted in sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: On Qingming, the mid-year festival, and the winter solstice, imperial sons-in-law were dispatched separately to lead the rite, with civil and military officials assisting.

sentences.zh: 忌辰及正旦、孟冬、聖節，亦遣駙馬都尉行禮。

translations.literal: On death anniversaries and on New Year's Day, mid-winter, and the emperor's birthday, sons-in-law of the emperor were also dispatched to perform the rite.
translations.idiomatic: On death anniversaries, New Year's Day, mid-winter, and the emperor's birthday, sons-in-law were likewise dispatched.

sentences.zh: 親王之籓，詣諸陵辭謁。

translations.literal: When princes went to their fiefs, they took leave and visited the various mausoleums.
translations.idiomatic: Princes departing for their fiefs paid respects and took leave at the mausoleums.

sentences.zh: 恭讓章皇后陵，清明、中元、冬至、忌辰內官行禮。

translations.literal: At the mausoleum of Empress Zhangrang, Qingming, the mid-year festival, the winter solstice, and death anniversaries were performed by inner-palace eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: At Empress Zhangrang's tomb, Qingming, the mid-year festival, the winter solstice, and death anniversaries were conducted by inner-palace eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 西山景皇帝陵，祭期如上，儀賓行禮。

translations.literal: At the tomb of Emperor Jing in the Western Hills, the sacrificial schedule was as above, with ritual guests performing the rite.
translations.idiomatic: At Emperor Jing's Western Hills tomb the calendar matched the above, with ritual guests performing the rite.

sentences.zh: 初，成祖易黃土山名天壽山。

translations.literal: At first, Chengzu changed the name of Huangtu Mountain to Tianshou Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Originally Chengzu renamed Huangtu Mountain Tianshou Mountain.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十年，名祖陵曰基運山，皇陵曰翌聖山，孝陵曰神烈山，顯陵曰純德山，及天壽山，並方澤從祀，所在有司祭告各陵山祇。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Jiajing, Zuling's mountain was named Jiyun Mountain, the imperial mausoleum's Yisheng Mountain, Xiaoling's Shenlie Mountain, Xianling's Chunde Mountain, and Tianshou Mountain—all were added to the square-altar collateral sacrifice; local officials made sacrificial announcement to the spirit of each mausoleum mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing year 10, Zuling's mountain was named Jiyun, the imperial tomb's Yisheng, Xiaoling's Shenlie, Xianling's Chunde, and Tianshou Mountain—all joined the square-altar collateral sacrifice, and local officials reported to each mausoleum mountain spirit.

sentences.zh: 禮官因奏：「神祇壇每年秋祭，有鐘山、天壽山之神，今宜增基運等山。

translations.literal: The ritual officials therefore memorialized: "At the annual autumn sacrifice at the Spirits Altar, there are the spirits of Zhong Mountain and Tianshou Mountain; now Jiyun and the other mountains should be added.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officials memorialized: "The Spirits Altar autumn sacrifice already includes Zhong and Tianshou mountains; Jiyun and the others should now be added.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The proposal was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: " Approved.

sentences.zh: 十四年，諭禮部尚書夏言：「清明節既遣官上陵，內殿復祭，似涉煩復。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, the emperor instructed Minister of Rites Xia Yan: "On Qingming, after officials are already sent to the mausoleum, the inner hall sacrifices again—this seems redundant.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14 the emperor told Minister of Rites Xia Yan: "On Qingming we already send officials to the mausoleum, yet the inner hall sacrifices again—it seems redundant.

sentences.zh: 」言因言：「我朝祀典，如特享、時享、祫享、禘祭，足應經義，可爲世法。

translations.literal: " Yan therefore said: "Our dynasty's sacrificial canon—such as special offerings, seasonal offerings, collective offerings, and Di sacrifice—fully accords with classical meaning and may serve as a model for the age.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan replied: "Our sacrificial canon—special, seasonal, collective, and Di offerings—fully meets classical doctrine and can model the age.

sentences.zh: 惟上陵及奉先殿多沿前代故事。

translations.literal: Only visiting the mausoleum and the Hall of Ancestors largely follow former dynasties' precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Only mausoleum visits and the Hall of Ancestors largely follow earlier dynasties.

sentences.zh: 上陵之祀，每歲清明、中元、冬至凡三。

translations.literal: Mausoleum sacrifice occurs three times each year: Qingming, the mid-year festival, and the winter solstice.
translations.idiomatic: Mausoleum rites were held thrice yearly: Qingming, the mid-year festival, and the winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 中元俗節，事本不經。

translations.literal: The mid-year festival is a popular observance without classical basis.
translations.idiomatic: The mid-year festival is a folk observance without canonical warrant.

sentences.zh: 往因郊祀在正首，故冬至上陵，蓋重一氣之始，伸報本之義。

translations.literal: Formerly because suburban sacrifice fell at the start of the year, winter solstice mausoleum visits were made—honoring the beginning of qi and extending the meaning of repaying the root.
translations.idiomatic: Because suburban sacrifice once fell at year's start, winter solstice mausoleum visits honored the beginning of cosmic qi and expressed repayment to one's root.

sentences.zh: 今冬至既行大報配天之禮，則陵事爲輕。

translations.literal: Now that the winter solstice already has the great report and matching Heaven sacrifice, mausoleum affairs are lighter.
translations.idiomatic: Now the winter solstice already has the great report and matching-Heaven rite, so mausoleum duties weigh less.

sentences.zh: 況有事南郊，乃輟陪祀臣僚，遠出山陵，恐於尊祖配天之誠未盡。

translations.literal: Moreover, when there are affairs at the southern suburban altar, to withdraw assisting ministers far to the mountain mausoleums may not fully express reverence for honoring ancestors and matching Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When the southern suburban rite is underway, pulling assisting ministers away to distant mausoleums may fall short of reverence toward ancestors and Heaven.

sentences.zh: 可罷冬至上陵，而移中元於霜降，惟清明如舊。

translations.literal: Winter solstice mausoleum visits may be abolished, and the mid-year festival moved to Frost's Descent; only Qingming remains as before.
translations.idiomatic: Winter solstice mausoleum visits may be dropped; move the mid-year rite to Frost's Descent; keep Qingming unchanged.

sentences.zh: 蓋清明禮行於春，所謂雨露既濡，君子履之，有怵惕之心者也。

translations.literal: For Qingming rites fall in spring—what is called "when dew and rain have moistened it, the gentleman treads upon it with a heart of fear and caution."
translations.idiomatic: Qingming falls in spring—"when dew and rain have soaked the ground, the gentleman walks upon it with wary reverence."

sentences.zh: 霜降禮行於秋，所謂霜露既降，君子履之，有悽愴之心者也。

translations.literal: Frost's Descent rites fall in autumn—what is called "when frost and dew have fallen, the gentleman treads upon it with a heart of sorrow and grief."
translations.idiomatic: Frost's Descent falls in autumn—"when frost and dew have descended, the gentleman walks upon it with sorrowful grief."

sentences.zh: 二節既遣官上陵，則內殿之祭，誠不宜復。

translations.literal: When both festivals already dispatch officials to the mausoleum, inner-hall sacrifice truly should not be repeated.
translations.idiomatic: Once officials are sent to the mausoleum on both days, inner-hall sacrifice should indeed not be repeated.

sentences.zh: 」遂著爲令。

translations.literal: " This was then fixed as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: " This was enacted as statute.

sentences.zh: 十五年，諭言曰：「廟重於陵，其禮嚴。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, the emperor instructed Yan: "The temple is weightier than the mausoleum; its ritual is stricter.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 the emperor told Yan: "The temple outweighs the mausoleum; its rites are stricter.

sentences.zh: 故廟中一帝一後，陵則二三後配葬。

translations.literal: Therefore in the temple one emperor and one empress; at the mausoleum two or three empresses may be buried in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the temple holds one emperor and one empress, while the mausoleum may receive two or three consorts in attendant burial.

sentences.zh: 今別建奉慈殿，不若奉主於陵殿爲宜。

translations.literal: Now to build a separate Hall of Fond Memory is not as fitting as installing the tablets in the mausoleum hall.
translations.idiomatic: Building a separate Hall of Fond Memory is less fitting than enshrining the tablets in the mausoleum hall.

sentences.zh: 且梓宮配葬，而主乃別置，近於黜之，非親之也。

translations.literal: Moreover the coffin is buried in attendance while the tablet is placed elsewhere—this approaches dismissal and is not treating them as kin.
translations.idiomatic: When the coffin shares burial but the tablet is set apart, that nears dismissal and is not kinship.

sentences.zh: 」乃遷孝肅、孝穆、孝惠三後神主於陵殿。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the spirit tablets of the three empresses Xiaosu, Xiaomu, and Xiaohui were moved to the mausoleum hall.
translations.idiomatic: " The spirit tablets of Empresses Xiaosu, Xiaomu, and Xiaohui were then moved to the mausoleum hall.

sentences.zh: 又諭言曰：「三後神主稱皇太后、太皇太后者，乃子孫所奉尊稱。

translations.literal: The emperor again instructed Yan: "Calling the three empresses' tablets Empress Dowager and Grand Empress Dowager are honorific titles bestowed by descendants.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again told Yan: "Titles of Empress Dowager and Grand Empress Dowager on the three tablets are honorifics given by descendants.

sentences.zh: 今既遷陵殿，則名實不準。

translations.literal: Now that they have been moved to the mausoleum hall, name and reality do not accord.
translations.idiomatic: Now that they rest in the mausoleum hall, title and fact no longer align.

sentences.zh: 」言等議曰：「三後神主，禮不祔廟，義當從祧。

translations.literal: " Yan and others deliberated: "The three empresses' tablets, by ritual not enshrined in the temple, should follow removal to the distant shrine.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan and colleagues argued: "These three tablets, not enshrined in the temple by rite, should follow distant-shrine removal.

sentences.zh: 遷奉陵殿，深合典禮。

translations.literal: Moving them to the mausoleum hall deeply accords with canonical ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Transfer to the mausoleum hall deeply fits canonical ritual.

sentences.zh: 其稱皇太后、太皇太后者，乃子孫所上尊號。

translations.literal: Calling them Empress Dowager and Grand Empress Dowager are honorific titles raised by descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager and Grand Empress Dowager are descendant-bestowed honorifics.

sentences.zh: 今已遷奉於陵，則當從夫婦之義，改題孝肅神主，不用睿字，孝穆、孝惠神主，俱不用純字，則嫡庶有別，而尊親並隆矣。

translations.literal: Now that they have been moved to the mausoleum, they should follow the husband-and-wife principle: revise Xiaosu's tablet without the character Rui; Xiaomu's and Xiaohui's tablets both without the character Chun—then primary and secondary wives are distinguished while honoring kin alike.
translations.idiomatic: At the mausoleum they should follow husband-and-wife usage: Xiaosu's tablet should drop the character Rui; Xiaomu's and Xiaohui's should drop Chun—distinguishing primary from secondary while honoring both.

sentences.zh: 」命如擬行。

translations.literal: " An order was given to proceed as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: " The court ordered implementation as proposed.

sentences.zh: 又諭：「祭告長陵等七陵俱躬叩拜，恭讓章皇后、景皇帝陵亦展拜一次，以慰追感之情。

translations.literal: The emperor again instructed: "In announcing sacrifice at the seven mausoleums including Changling, all shall personally kowtow; at Empress Zhangrang's and Emperor Jing's mausoleums also perform one extended bow, to comfort the feeling of retrospective longing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also ordered: "When announcing sacrifice at the seven mausoleums including Changling, I shall kowtow in person; at Empress Zhangrang's and Emperor Jing's tombs perform one extended bow to ease retrospective grief.

sentences.zh: 」十七年，改陵殿曰祾恩殿，門曰祾恩門。

translations.literal: " In the seventeenth year, the mausoleum hall was renamed Hall of Blessing and Grace, and the gate Blessing and Grace Gate.
translations.idiomatic: " In year 17 the mausoleum hall was renamed Hall of Blessing and Grace and its gate Blessing and Grace Gate.

sentences.zh: 又建成祖聖蹟亭於平臺山，率從官行祭禮。

translations.literal: Also the Holy Traces Pavilion of Chengzu was built on Pingtai Mountain, and the emperor led attendant officials in performing sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzu's Holy Traces Pavilion was also built on Pingtai Mountain, where the emperor led attendants in sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，工部尚書顧璘請以帝所上顯陵聖制歌詩，製爲樂章，享獻陵廟。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, Minister of Works Gu Lin requested that the emperor's sacred compositions and poems for Xianling be made into ritual hymns and offered at the mausoleum temple.
translations.idiomatic: In year 21 Minister of Works Gu Lin asked that the emperor's sacred poems for Xianling be set as ritual hymns for mausoleum offering.

sentences.zh: 禮部言： 「天壽山諸陵，歲祀皆不用樂。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites said: "At the various Tianshou Mountain mausoleums, annual sacrifice never uses music.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites replied: "Annual sacrifice at Tianshou mausoleums never employs music.

sentences.zh: 」已而承天府守備太監傅霖乞增顯陵歲暮之祭。

translations.literal: " Shortly afterward the Fengyang guard eunuch Fu Lin requested adding a year-end sacrifice at Xianling.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon after, the Shuntian guard eunuch Fu Lin asked to add a year-end sacrifice at Xianling.

sentences.zh: 部議言：「諸陵皆無歲暮祀典。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated: "None of the mausoleums has a year-end sacrificial precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry replied: "No mausoleum has a year-end sacrificial precedent.

sentences.zh: 」詔並從部議。

translations.literal: " An edict approved the ministry's deliberation in both cases.
translations.idiomatic: " The throne approved the ministry on both matters.

sentences.zh: 隆慶二年，帝詣天壽山春祭。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longqing, the emperor went to Tianshou Mountain for the spring sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing year 2 the emperor went to Tianshou Mountain for spring sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 前一日，告世宗几筵及奉先、弘孝、神霄殿。

translations.literal: On the previous day he announced at Shizong's spirit seat and at the Halls of Ancestors, Hongxiao, and Divine Empyrean.
translations.idiomatic: The day before he announced at Shizong's spirit seat and at the Ancestors, Hongxiao, and Divine Empyrean halls.

sentences.zh: 駕至天壽山紅門降輿，由左門入，升輿，駐蹕感思殿。

translations.literal: When the imperial procession reached Tianshou Mountain's Red Gate he descended from the carriage, entered by the left gate, mounted again, and halted at the Hall of Reflective Thought.
translations.idiomatic: At Tianshou Mountain's Red Gate he left the carriage, entered by the left gate, remounted, and halted at the Hall of Reflective Thought.

sentences.zh: 越二日，質明行禮。

translations.literal: After two days, at dawn the ritual was performed.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later, at dawn, the rite was performed.

sentences.zh: 帝青袍，乘板輿至長陵門外，東降輿，由殿左門入，至拜位，上香，四拜。

translations.literal: The emperor in a blue robe rode a palanquin to outside Changling's gate, descended on the east, entered by the hall's left gate, reached the bowing position, offered incense, and bowed four times.
translations.idiomatic: In a blue robe he rode a palanquin to Changling's outer gate, descended on the east, entered the hall's left gate, offered incense at the bowing place, and bowed four times.

sentences.zh: 至神御前獻帛、獻爵訖，復位。

translations.literal: Before the spirit seat he presented silk and poured the libation, then returned to position.
translations.idiomatic: Before the spirit seat he presented silk and libation, then returned to place.

sentences.zh: 亞獻、終獻，令執爵者代，復四拜。

translations.literal: For secondary and final offerings, the cup-bearer substituted; he bowed four times again.
translations.idiomatic: Secondary and final offerings were poured by attendants; he bowed four times again.

sentences.zh: 餘如常祭之儀。

translations.literal: The remainder followed the usual sacrifice ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The rest followed ordinary sacrificial form.

sentences.zh: 隨詣永陵行禮。

translations.literal: He then proceeded to Yongling to perform the rite.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to Yongling to perform the rite.

sentences.zh: 是日遣官六員，俱青服，分祭六陵。

translations.literal: That day six officials in blue robes were dispatched to sacrifice separately at the six mausoleums.
translations.idiomatic: That day six officials in blue were dispatched to sacrifice at six mausoleums separately.

sentences.zh: 萬曆八年，謁陵禮如舊。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Wanli, the mausoleum-visiting ritual was as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli year 8 mausoleum visits followed the old form.

sentences.zh: 十一年，復謁陵。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, mausoleum visits were resumed.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 mausoleum visits were resumed.

sentences.zh: 禮部言：「宜遵世宗彝憲，酌分二日，以次展拜。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites said: "It is fitting to follow Shizong's constant statute, apportioning over two days and bowing in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites said: "Follow Shizong's standing rule: spread over two days and bow in sequence.

sentences.zh: 」乃定長、永、昭三陵，上香，八拜，親奠帛。

translations.literal: " It was then fixed that at the three mausoleums Chang, Yong, and Zhao, incense was offered with eight bows and the emperor personally presented silk.
translations.idiomatic: " It was fixed: at Chang, Yong, and Zhao mausoleums, incense with eight bows and the emperor's personal silk offering.

sentences.zh: 初獻，六陵二寢，上香，四拜。

translations.literal: At the initial offering, the six mausoleums and two chambers received incense with four bows.
translations.idiomatic: At the initial offering, the six mausoleums and two chambers received incense with four bows.

sentences.zh: 其奠帛三獻，俱執事官代。

translations.literal: Presentation of silk and the three libations were all performed by attending officials.
translations.idiomatic: Silk presentation and the three libations were all performed by attending officials.

sentences.zh: 十四年，禮部言：「諸妃葬金山諸處者，嘉靖中俱配享各陵殿，罷本墳祭。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, the Ministry of Rites said: "Consorts buried at Jinshan and other places were in Jiajing all given collateral enjoyment at each mausoleum hall, and sacrifice at their own tombs was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14 the Ministry said: "Consorts buried at Jinshan and elsewhere were in Jiajing given collateral enjoyment at each mausoleum hall and their own tomb sacrifices ended.

sentences.zh: 今世廟諸妃安厝西山者，宜從其例。

translations.literal: Now consorts enshrined at the Western Hills in the present imperial temple should follow that precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Consorts now enshrined at the Western Hills should follow that precedent.

sentences.zh: 至陵祭品物，九陵、恭讓、恭仁之陵止於酒果，而越、靖諸王及諸王妃則又有牲果祝文，反從其厚者，蓋以九陵帝后，歲暮已祫祭於廟，旬日內且復有孟春之享，故元旦陵殿止用酒果，非儉也；

translations.literal: As for mausoleum sacrificial goods, the nine mausoleums and the tombs of Zhangrang and Gongren used only wine and fruit, while the Yue, Jing princes and their consorts also had victims, fruit, and prayer text—contrary to the fuller practice—because for the nine mausoleums the emperor and empresses already had collective temple sacrifice at year-end, and within ten days there would again be the mid-spring offering; therefore on New Year's Day the mausoleum hall used only wine and fruit, not from frugality.
translations.idiomatic: Mausoleum offerings differed: the nine imperial tombs and Zhangrang and Gongren used only wine and fruit, while Yue, Jing princes and consorts received victims, fruit, and prayer text—seemingly richer—because the nine tombs' emperor and empresses already had year-end collective temple rites and mid-spring offering within ten days, so New Year's mausoleum halls used only wine and fruit, not from austerity;

sentences.zh: 諸王諸妃則祫祭春祭皆不與，元旦一祭不宜從簡，故用牲帛祝文，非豐也。

translations.literal: Princes and consorts did not share in collective or spring temple sacrifice; one New Year's mausoleum sacrifice should not be simplified, hence victims, silk, and prayer text—not from abundance.
translations.idiomatic: princes and consorts had neither collective nor spring temple rites, so one New Year's mausoleum rite should not be reduced—hence victims, silk, and prayer text, not from lavishness.

sentences.zh: 特恭讓、恭仁既不與祫享於廟中，又不設牲帛於陵殿，是則禮文之缺，宜增所未備。

translations.literal: Yet Zhangrang and Gongren had neither collective enjoyment in the temple nor victims and silk at the mausoleum hall—this is a gap in ritual text; what is not yet provided should be added.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhangrang and Gongren had neither temple collective enjoyment nor mausoleum victims and silk—a lacuna in ritual text that should be supplied.

sentences.zh: 而諸王諸妃祝文，尚仍安厝時所用，宜改敘歲時遣官之意，則情順禮安。

translations.literal: As for the prayer texts of princes and consorts, they still use those from the time of temporary enshrinement; they should be revised to express the meaning of dispatching officials at the seasonal times, then feeling and ritual will be harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: The prayer texts for princes and consorts still follow wording from temporary enshrinement; they should be revised to reflect annual official dispatch, so sentiment and ritual align.

sentences.zh: 」報可。

translations.literal: " The reply was approval.
translations.idiomatic: " Approved.

sentences.zh: 凡山陵規制，有寶城，長陵最大，徑一百一丈八尺。

translations.literal: As for the regulations of mountain mausoleums, there is the treasure city; Changling is largest, with a diameter of one hundred and one zhang eight chi.
translations.idiomatic: Mausoleum layout includes a treasure city; Changling's is largest, one hundred one zhang eight chi in diameter.

sentences.zh: 次永陵，徑八十一丈。

translations.literal: Next is Yongling, with a diameter of eighty-one zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Yongling follows at eighty-one zhang diameter.

sentences.zh: 各陵深廣丈尺有差。

translations.literal: Each mausoleum's depth and breadth in zhang and chi differ.
translations.idiomatic: Depth and breadth differ for each tomb.

sentences.zh: 正前爲明樓，樓中立帝廟諡石碑，下爲靈寢門。

translations.literal: Directly in front is the Bright Tower; within the tower stands the imperial temple posthumous-title stone tablet; below is the Spirit Sleeping Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The facade Bright Tower holds the temple posthumous-title stele; below lies the Spirit Sleeping Gate.

sentences.zh: 惟永陵中爲券門。

translations.literal: Only Yongling has an arched gate in the center.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yongling centers an arched gate.

sentences.zh: 左右牆門各一樓。

translations.literal: On left and right wall gates, each has one tower.
translations.idiomatic: Each side wall gate has its own tower.

sentences.zh: 明樓前爲石几筵，又前爲祾恩殿、祾恩門。

translations.literal: Before the Bright Tower is the stone offering table; still before are the Hall of Blessing and Grace and Blessing and Grace Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Bright Tower stand stone offering tables, then the Hall and Gate of Blessing and Grace.

sentences.zh: 殿惟長陵重檐九間，左右配殿各十五間。

translations.literal: The hall: only Changling has double eaves and nine bays; left and right side halls each fifteen bays.
translations.idiomatic: Changling alone has double eaves and nine bays, with fifteen-bay side halls each.

sentences.zh: 永陵重檐七間，配殿各九間。

translations.literal: Yongling has double eaves and seven bays; side halls each nine bays.
translations.idiomatic: Yongling has seven bays with double eaves and nine-bay side halls.

sentences.zh: 諸陵俱殿五間，配殿五間。

translations.literal: All other mausoleums have five-bay halls and five-bay side halls.
translations.idiomatic: Other mausoleums use five-bay halls and matching side halls.

sentences.zh: 門外神庫或一或二，神廚宰牲亭，有聖蹟碑亭。

translations.literal: Outside the gate are one or two spirit storehouses, spirit kitchens and slaughter pavilions, and Holy Traces stele pavilions.
translations.idiomatic: Outside stand one or two spirit storehouses, spirit kitchens, slaughter pavilions, and Holy Traces stele pavilions.

sentences.zh: 諸陵碑俱設門外，率無字。

translations.literal: All mausoleum steles are set outside the gate and generally bear no characters.
translations.idiomatic: Mausoleum steles sit outside the gate, usually blank.

sentences.zh: 長陵迤南有總神道，有石橋，有石像人物十八對，擎天柱四，石望柱二。

translations.literal: South of Changling extends the general spirit way, with stone bridges, eighteen pairs of stone figures, four heaven-supporting pillars, and two stone watching pillars.
translations.idiomatic: South of Changling runs the collective spirit way with stone bridges, eighteen pairs of stone figures, four heaven pillars, and two watching pillars.

sentences.zh: 長陵有《神功聖德碑》，仁宗御撰，在神道正南。

translations.literal: Changling has the Stele of Divine Merit and Sagely Virtue, composed by Renzong, directly south on the spirit way.
translations.idiomatic: Changling bears Renzong's Stele of Divine Merit and Sagely Virtue on the spirit way's south axis.

sentences.zh: 南爲紅門，門外石牌坊一。

translations.literal: South is the Red Gate; outside the gate one stone memorial arch.
translations.idiomatic: South lies the Red Gate with one stone memorial arch outside.

sentences.zh: 門內有時陟殿，爲車駕更衣之所。

translations.literal: Within the gate is the Timely Ascent Hall, where the imperial carriage changes dress.
translations.idiomatic: Inside is the Timely Ascent Hall for changing imperial dress.

sentences.zh: 永陵稍東有感思殿，爲駐蹕之所。

translations.literal: Slightly east of Yongling is the Hall of Reflective Thought, where the procession halts.
translations.idiomatic: East of Yongling stands the Hall of Reflective Thought as the halting place.

sentences.zh: 殿東爲神馬廠。

translations.literal: East of the hall is the divine horse depot.
translations.idiomatic: East of the hall lies the divine horse depot.

sentences.zh: ○忌辰

translations.literal: ○ Death anniversary
translations.idiomatic: ○ On death anniversaries

sentences.zh: 洪武八年四月，仁祖忌日，太祖親詣皇陵致祭。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eighth year of Hongwu, on the death anniversary of Renzu, Taizu personally went to the imperial mausoleum to offer sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 8, fourth month, on Renzu's death anniversary Taizu sacrificed in person at the imperial mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年，禮部尚書李至剛等奏定，高皇帝忌辰前二日，帝服淺淡色衣，御西角門視事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongle, Minister of Rites Li Zhigang and others memorialized and fixed: two days before the death anniversary of the High Emperor, the emperor wears pale-colored garments and conducts affairs at the West Corner Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle year 1, Minister of Rites Li Zhigang fixed that two days before the High Emperor's death anniversary the emperor wears pale dress and holds court at the West Corner Gate.

sentences.zh: 不鳴鐘鼓，不行賞罰，不舉音樂，禁屠宰。

translations.literal: Bells and drums are not sounded; rewards and punishments are not carried out; music is not performed; slaughter is forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: No bells or drums, rewards or punishments, or music; slaughter is forbidden.

sentences.zh: 百官淺淡色衣、黑角帶朝參。

translations.literal: All officials wear pale-colored garments and black horn belts for court attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Officials attend in pale dress with black horn belts.

sentences.zh: 至日，親祀於奉先殿，仍率百官詣孝陵致祭。

translations.literal: On the day itself, the emperor sacrifices in person at the Hall of Ancestors and still leads all officials to Xiaoling to offer sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he sacrifices at the Hall of Ancestors and leads officials to Xiaoling.

sentences.zh: 高皇后忌辰如之。

translations.literal: The death anniversary of the High Empress was the same.
translations.idiomatic: The High Empress's anniversary followed the same rule.

sentences.zh: 宣德四年令，凡遇忌辰，通政司、禮科、兵馬司勿引囚奏事。

translations.literal: An order of the fourth year of Xuande: whenever a death anniversary occurs, the Office of Transmission, the Rites Section, and the Horse Patrol Office shall not present prisoners for judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Xuande year 4: on death anniversaries the Transmission Office, Rites Section, and Horse Patrol must not present prisoners.

sentences.zh: 五年，敕百官朝參輟奏事儀。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, an edict ordered officials at court attendance to suspend memorializing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 an edict suspended memorials during anniversary attendance.

sentences.zh: 英宗即位，召禮臣及翰林院議忌辰禮。

translations.literal: When Yingzong took the throne, he summoned ritual officials and the Hanlin Academy to deliberate death-anniversary ritual.
translations.idiomatic: At Yingzong's accession he summoned ritualists and Hanlin to fix anniversary rites.

sentences.zh: 大學士楊士奇、楊榮，學士楊溥議：「每歲高廟帝后、文廟帝后、仁宗忌辰，服淺淡色服，不鳴鐘鼓，於奉天門視事。

translations.literal: Grand Secretaries Yang Shiqi and Yang Rong and academician Yang Pu deliberated: "Each year on the death anniversaries of the High Temple emperor and empresses, Wenzong emperor and empresses, and Renzong, wear pale-colored garments, do not sound bells and drums, and conduct affairs at Fengtian Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi, Rong, and Pu proposed: on High Temple, Wenzong, and Renzong anniversaries wear pale dress, silence bells and drums, and hold court at Fengtian Gate.

sentences.zh: 宣宗忌辰，小祥之日，於西角門視事。

translations.literal: On Xuandezong's death anniversary, on the day of lesser felicity, conduct affairs at the West Corner Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On Xuandezong's anniversary, on the lesser mourning day, hold court at the West Corner Gate.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The proposal was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: " Approved.

sentences.zh: 弘治十四年令，凡遇忌辰，朝參官不得服糹寧絲紗羅衣。

translations.literal: An order of the fourteenth year of Hongzhi: whenever a death anniversary occurs, attending officials may not wear silk gauze or damask garments.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi year 14: anniversary attendees may not wear silk gauze or damask.

sentences.zh: 景皇帝、恭讓皇后忌辰，遇節令，服青絲花樣。

translations.literal: On the death anniversaries of Emperor Jing and Empress Zhangrang, when a festival day coincides, wear blue silk with floral pattern.
translations.idiomatic: On Jing and Zhangrang anniversaries that fall on festivals, wear blue floral silk.

sentences.zh: 宣宗忌辰，遇祭祀，服紅。

translations.literal: On Xuandezong's death anniversary, when sacrifice occurs, wear red.
translations.idiomatic: On Xuandezong's anniversary during sacrifice, wear red.

sentences.zh: 十六年八月，吏部尚書馬文升言：「宣德間，仁宗忌辰，諸司悉免奏事。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the sixteenth year, Minister of Personnel Ma Wensheng said: "In the Xuande period, on Renzong's death anniversary all offices entirely ceased presenting memorials.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16, eighth month, Ma Wensheng said: "Under Xuande, Renzong's anniversary halted all memorials.

sentences.zh: 自太祖至仁宗生忌，俱輟朝。

translations.literal: From Taizu through Renzong's birth anniversaries, court was all suspended.
translations.idiomatic: From Taizu through Renzong, birth anniversaries suspended court.

sentences.zh: 其後不知何時，仁宗忌辰，依前奏事。

translations.literal: Afterward, at some unknown time, on Renzong's death anniversary memorials were presented as before.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at some point, Renzong's death anniversary again allowed memorials.

sentences.zh: 惟太祖至憲宗忌辰，百官淺淡色服、黑角帶。

translations.literal: Only from Taizu through Xianzong's death anniversaries did officials wear pale-colored garments and black horn belts.
translations.idiomatic: Only from Taizu through Xianzong death anniversaries required pale dress and black horn belts.

sentences.zh: 朝廷亦出視朝，鳴鐘鼓，奏事。

translations.literal: The court also held audience, sounded bells and drums, and heard affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Court still held audience, bells, drums, and business.

sentences.zh: 臣思自仁至憲，世有遠近，服有隆殺。

translations.literal: Your subject reflects that from Ren to Xian generations differ in distance, and garments differ in gradation of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Generations from Ren to Xian differ in distance; mourning gradation should differ too.

sentences.zh: 請自仁宗忌辰、英宗生忌日，視朝，鳴鐘鼓。

translations.literal: Request that from Renzong's death anniversary and Yingzong's birth anniversary, hold audience and sound bells and drums.
translations.idiomatic: From Renzong's death anniversary and Yingzong's birth anniversary, hold full audience with bells and drums.

sentences.zh: 若遇憲宗及孝穆皇太后忌日，不視朝，著淺淡服，進素膳，不預他事。

translations.literal: If it is Xianzong's or Empress Dowager Xiaomu's death anniversary, do not hold audience; wear pale garments, serve plain food, and take no other affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On Xianzong or Xiaomu anniversaries, skip audience; wear pale dress, plain food, no other business.

sentences.zh: 或遵宣宗時例，自太祖至憲宗生忌，俱輟朝一日。

translations.literal: Or follow the Xuande precedent: from Taizu through Xianzong birth anniversaries, all suspend court one day.
translations.idiomatic: Or follow Xuande: suspend court one day for Taizu through Xianzong birth anniversaries.

sentences.zh: 憲宗、孝穆忌日，如臣所擬。

translations.literal: Xianzong and Xiaomu death anniversaries as your subject proposes.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong and Xiaomu death anniversaries per my proposal.

sentences.zh: 」帝下禮部議。

translations.literal: " The emperor referred it to the Ministry of Rites for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor sent it to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 部臣言：「經傳所載，忌日爲親死之日。

translations.literal: Ministry officials said: "The classics record that the day of taboo is the day of a parent's death.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry cited classics: taboo day means the day of death.

sentences.zh: 則死日爲忌，非謂生辰也。

translations.literal: Thus the day of death is taboo, not the day of birth.
translations.idiomatic: Taboo marks death, not birth.

sentences.zh: 其曰忌日不用，不以此日爲他事也。

translations.literal: It says on taboo days one does not use them—for other affairs on that day.
translations.idiomatic: Taboo days forbid other business.

sentences.zh: 曰忌日不樂，是不可舉吉事也，此日當專意哀思父母，餘事皆不舉。

translations.literal: It says on taboo days one does not rejoice—auspicious affairs may not be undertaken; on this day one should focus grief on parents and undertake nothing else.
translations.idiomatic: Taboo days forbid joyous affairs; one should mourn parents exclusively.

sentences.zh: 但先朝事例，迄今見行，未敢更易。

translations.literal: But former-court precedents continue in practice today; we dare not change them lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Former precedents still run; we dare not change lightly.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃酌定以淺淡服色視事。

translations.literal: " The emperor then settled on conducting affairs in pale-colored garments.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor fixed pale dress while conducting affairs.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖七年令，忌辰只祭本位。

translations.literal: An order of the seventh year of Jiajing: on death anniversaries sacrifice only the principal tablet.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing year 7: anniversary sacrifice only at the principal seat.

sentences.zh: 十八年令，高廟帝后忌辰祭於景神殿，列聖帝后忌辰祭於永孝殿。

translations.literal: An order of the eighteenth year: High Temple emperor and empress death anniversaries sacrifice at the Jing Spirit Hall; successive emperors and empresses sacrifice at the Eternal Filiality Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing year 18: High Temple anniversaries at Jing Spirit Hall; successive emperors at Eternal Filiality Hall.

sentences.zh: 二十四年令，仍祭於奉先殿。

translations.literal: An order of the twenty-fourth year: sacrifice again at the Hall of Ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing year 24: sacrifice returned to the Hall of Ancestors.

sentences.zh: ○乘輿受蕃國王訃奏儀

translations.literal: ○ Protocol for the imperial carriage receiving death notices from tributary kings
translations.idiomatic: ○ Protocol for the throne receiving tributary kings' obituaries

sentences.zh: 凡蕃國王薨，使者訃奏至，於西華門內壬地設御幄，皇帝素服乘輿詣幄。

translations.literal: Whenever a tributary king dies and the envoy's death notice arrives, an imperial canopy is set within Xihua Gate on ren ground; the emperor in plain dress rides the carriage to the canopy.
translations.idiomatic: When a tributary king dies and the obituary envoy arrives, a canopy is set inside Xihua Gate; the emperor in plain dress proceeds there.

sentences.zh: 太常卿奏：「某國世子遣陪臣某官某，奏某國王臣某薨。

translations.literal: The Director of Imperial Sacrifices announces: "The heir of such country has dispatched accompanying minister such-and-such official, reporting that King such-and-such of such country has died.
translations.idiomatic: The Director announces: "The heir of [state] sent minister [name] to report King [name]'s death.

sentences.zh: 」承製官至使者前宣制曰：「皇帝致問爾某國王某，得何疾而逝。

translations.literal: " The edict-receiver reaches the envoy and proclaims: "The emperor sends inquiry to your King such-and-such of such country—what illness did he die of.
translations.idiomatic: " The edict officer asks: "The emperor inquires what illness took your king.

sentences.zh: 」使者答故。

translations.literal: " The envoy answers as to the cause.
translations.idiomatic: " The envoy answers regarding the cause.

sentences.zh: 其儀大略如臨王公大臣喪儀，但不舉哀。

translations.literal: The ritual is largely like attending the funeral of princes and great ministers, but lamentation is not raised.
translations.idiomatic: The rite largely matches attendance at princely funerals, without raised lamentation.

sentences.zh: 凡塞外都督等官訃至，永樂間遣官齎香鈔諭祭。

translations.literal: Whenever death notices arrive from commanders and other officials beyond the passes, in the Yongle period officials were dispatched bearing incense and paper to announce sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: For frontier commanders' deaths, Yongle sent officials with incense and paper to announce sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 後定例，因其奏請，給與表裏祭文，令攜歸自祭。

translations.literal: Later the fixed precedent: according to their memorial request, grant robes and sacrificial text for them to carry home and sacrifice themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Later precedent granted robes and sacrificial text on request for home sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 來京病故者，遣官諭祭或賜棺賜葬。

translations.literal: Those who died of illness in the capital were announced sacrifice by dispatched officials or granted coffin and burial.
translations.idiomatic: Those dying in the capital received envoy sacrifice or granted coffin and burial.

sentences.zh: 後定年終類奏，遣官祭之。

translations.literal: Later it was fixed that at year-end collective memorial, officials were dispatched to sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Later year-end collective reports triggered dispatched sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 若在邊歿於戰陣者，不拘此例。

translations.literal: If they died on the frontier in battle array, this precedent does not apply.
translations.idiomatic: Death in battle on the frontier was excepted.

sentences.zh: 凡外國使臣病故者，令所在官司賜棺及祭，或欲歸葬者聽。

translations.literal: Whenever foreign envoys died, the local office was ordered to grant coffin and sacrifice, or if they wished to return the body for burial, they were permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign envoys dying received local coffin and sacrifice, or permitted repatriation.

sentences.zh: ○乘輿爲王公大臣舉哀儀

translations.literal: ○ Protocol for the imperial carriage raising lamentation for princes and great ministers
translations.idiomatic: ○ Protocol for the throne raising lamentation for princes and senior ministers

sentences.zh: ○乘輿臨王公大臣喪儀

translations.literal: ○ Protocol for the imperial carriage attending the funeral of princes and great ministers
translations.idiomatic: ○ Protocol for the throne attending princely and senior ministers' funerals

sentences.zh: 凡王公大臣訃奏，太史監擇皇帝臨喪日期。

translations.literal: Whenever the death notice of a prince or great minister is presented, the Directorate of Astronomy selects the date for the emperor to attend the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: On princely or ministerial obituary, the Astronomical Directorate sets the emperor's attendance date.

sentences.zh: 拱衛司設大次於喪家大門外，設御座於正廳中。

translations.literal: The Imperial Guard sets a great tent outside the bereaved family's main gate and an imperial seat in the central hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Guard erects a great tent outside the gate and an imperial seat in the main hall.

sentences.zh: 有司設百官次於大次之左右。

translations.literal: The responsible office sets officials' tents to left and right of the great tent.
translations.idiomatic: Officials' tents are placed left and right of the great tent.

sentences.zh: 侍儀司設百官陪立位於廳前左右，引禮四人位於百官之北，東西向。

translations.literal: The Directorate of Ceremonies sets officials' standing positions to assist left and right before the hall; four ushering ritualists north of the officials, facing east and west.
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonies sets officials' flanking positions and four ushers north of them, east-west facing.

sentences.zh: 設喪主以下拜位於廳前，主婦以下哭位於殯北幔中。

translations.literal: The chief mourner's bowing position is set before the hall; the chief wife's wailing position in the curtain north of the bier.
translations.idiomatic: The chief mourner bows before the hall; the chief wife wails north of the bier within the curtain.

sentences.zh: 其日，鑾駕至大次，降輅，升輿，入易素服。

translations.literal: On that day the imperial procession reaches the great tent, descends from the carriage, mounts the palanquin, enters and changes to plain dress.
translations.idiomatic: That day the procession halts at the great tent, dismounts, mounts the palanquin, and dons plain dress.

sentences.zh: 百官皆易服，先入就廳前，分班侍立。

translations.literal: All officials also change dress, enter first, and take their divided positions before the hall to attend standing.
translations.idiomatic: Officials change dress, enter first, and stand in divided ranks before the hall.

sentences.zh: 御輿出次。

translations.literal: The imperial palanquin leaves the tent.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial palanquin emerges.

sentences.zh: 喪主以下免絰去杖，衰服，出迎於大門外。

translations.literal: The chief mourner and those below remove the mourning headband and staff, wear mourning garments, and go out to welcome outside the main gate.
translations.idiomatic: Mourners remove headband and staff, don mourning dress, and welcome outside the gate.

sentences.zh: 望見乘輿，止哭，再拜，入於門內之西。

translations.literal: Seeing the imperial carriage, they stop wailing, bow twice, and enter to the west within the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the carriage, they cease wailing, bow twice, and wait inside the gate to the west.

sentences.zh: 乘輿入門，將軍四人前導，四人後從。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage enters the gate; four generals lead in front, four follow behind.
translations.idiomatic: The carriage enters with four generals before and four behind.

sentences.zh: 入至正廳，降輿，升詣靈座前，百官班於後。

translations.literal: Entering to the central hall, descending from the palanquin, ascending before the spirit seat; officials rank behind.
translations.idiomatic: At the central hall he descends, ascends to the spirit seat, officials ranked behind.

sentences.zh: 皇帝哭，百官皆哭。

translations.literal: The emperor wails; all officials wail.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wails; all officials wail.

sentences.zh: 太常卿奏止哭，三上香，三祭酒。

translations.literal: The Director of Imperial Sacrifices announces cessation of wailing; thrice offers incense; thrice pours libation.
translations.idiomatic: The Director ends wailing, offers incense three times, pours libation three times.

sentences.zh: 出至正廳御座，主喪以下詣廳下拜位，再拜。

translations.literal: Exiting to the imperial seat in the central hall, the chief mourner and those below proceed to the bowing position below the hall and bow twice.
translations.idiomatic: He returns to the hall seat; mourners bow twice below the hall.

sentences.zh: 承製官詣喪主前云：「有制」。

translations.literal: The edict-officer reaches before the chief mourner and says: "There is an edict."
translations.idiomatic: The edict officer announces: "There is an edict."

sentences.zh: 喪主以下皆跪。

translations.literal: The chief mourner and those below all kneel.
translations.idiomatic: All mourners kneel.

sentences.zh: 宣制訖，皆再拜，退立於廳西。

translations.literal: When the edict is proclaimed, all bow twice and withdraw to stand west of the hall.
translations.idiomatic: After the edict all bow twice and stand west of the hall.

sentences.zh: 太常卿奏禮畢，皇帝升輿，出就大次，易服。

translations.literal: The Director announces the ritual complete; the emperor mounts the palanquin, exits to the great tent, and changes dress.
translations.idiomatic: The Director closes the rite; the emperor remounts, returns to the tent, and changes dress.

sentences.zh: 御輿出，喪主以下詣前再拜退。

translations.literal: When the imperial palanquin exits, the chief mourner and those below go forward and bow twice in withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: As the palanquin departs, mourners advance, bow twice, and withdraw.

sentences.zh: 皇帝降輿升輅，喪主杖哭而入。

translations.literal: The emperor descends from the palanquin and mounts the carriage; the chief mourner enters leaning on the staff and wailing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor remounts the carriage; the chief mourner enters with staff, wailing.

sentences.zh: 諸儀衛贊唱，大略如常。

translations.literal: The various guards and ushers chant announcements, largely as usual.
translations.idiomatic: Guards and ushers chant largely as on ordinary occasions.

sentences.zh: 其公、侯卒葬輟朝禮，洪武二十三年定。

translations.literal: The ritual of suspending court when dukes and marquises die and are buried was fixed in the twenty-third year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: Court suspension when dukes and marquises die or are buried was fixed in Hongwu year 23.

sentences.zh: 凡公、侯卒於家者，聞喪輟朝三日。

translations.literal: Whenever a duke or marquis dies at home, on hearing the bereavement court is suspended three days.
translations.idiomatic: A duke or marquis dying at home suspends court three days on report.

sentences.zh: 下葬，一日。

translations.literal: At burial, one day.
translations.idiomatic: Burial suspends court one day.

sentences.zh: 卒於外者，聞喪，一日。

translations.literal: If dying outside, on hearing the bereavement, one day.
translations.idiomatic: Death abroad suspends court one day on report.

sentences.zh: 柩至京，三日。

translations.literal: When the coffin reaches the capital, three days.
translations.idiomatic: Coffin arrival in the capital suspends court three days.

sentences.zh: 下葬，仍一日。

translations.literal: At burial, still one day.
translations.idiomatic: Burial again suspends one day.

sentences.zh: 凡輟朝之日，不鳴鐘鼓，各官淺淡色衣朝參。

translations.literal: On all days of suspended court, bells and drums are not sounded; each official attends in pale-colored garments.
translations.idiomatic: On suspension days no bells or drums; officials attend in pale dress.

sentences.zh: 初制，都督至都指揮卒，輟朝二日。

translations.literal: The initial regulation: when commanders-in-chief through regional commanders died, court was suspended two days.
translations.idiomatic: Originally regional commanders' deaths suspended court two days.

sentences.zh: 永樂後更定，惟公、侯、駙馬、伯及一品官，輟朝一日。

translations.literal: After Yongle it was re-fixed: only dukes, marquises, imperial sons-in-law, earls, and first-rank officials had court suspended one day.
translations.idiomatic: After Yongle the rule was revised—only dukes, marquises, imperial sons-in-law, earls, and first-rank officials suspended court one day.

sentences.zh: ○中宮爲父祖喪儀

translations.literal: ○ Protocol for the inner palace mourning for fathers and grandfathers
translations.idiomatic: ○ On inner-palace mourning for paternal ancestors

sentences.zh: 凡中宮父母薨，訃報太常寺，轉報內使監。

translations.literal: Whenever the parents of the inner palace died, death notice was reported to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and relayed to the Directorate of Palace Eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress's parents died, notice went to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and then the Palace Eunuchs Directorate.

sentences.zh: 前期，設薦於別殿東壁下，爲皇后舉哀位及內命婦以下哭位。

translations.literal: In advance, offering mats were set beneath the east wall of the separate hall as places for the empress to raise lamentation and for inner-palace titled ladies and those below to wail.
translations.idiomatic: Beforehand mats were placed under the separate hall's east wall for the empress's lamentation and the palace ladies' wailing stations.

sentences.zh: 皇后出詣別殿，內使監令奏：「考某官以某月某日薨」，母則云：「妣某夫人」，祖考、妣同。

translations.literal: The empress went out to the separate hall; the eunuch director announced: "Your late father, such-and-such official, died on such month and day"; for the mother it says: "Your late mother, Lady such-and-such"; for grandfather and grandmother it is the same.
translations.idiomatic: The empress proceeded to the separate hall; the eunuch director announced, "Your late father, Official X, died on such-and-such a date," or for the mother, "Your late mother, Lady X," likewise for grandparents.

sentences.zh: 皇后哭，內命婦以下皆哭盡哀。

translations.literal: The empress wailed; inner-palace titled ladies and those below all wailed to completion.
translations.idiomatic: The empress wailed; all palace ladies wailed to the full.

sentences.zh: 皇后問故，又哭盡哀。

translations.literal: The empress inquired the cause, and again wailed to completion.
translations.idiomatic: The empress asked how the death occurred and wailed again to completion.

sentences.zh: 乃素服，內命婦皆素服，止哭，還宮。

translations.literal: Then they donned plain dress; inner-palace titled ladies all donned plain dress, ceased wailing, and returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Then all put on plain dress, ceased wailing, and returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 內使監令奏聞。

translations.literal: The eunuch director reported to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch director memorialized the throne.

sentences.zh: 得旨：「皇后奔喪。

translations.literal: Receiving the decree: "The empress shall rush to the bereavement.
translations.idiomatic: Decree received: "The empress is to rush to the funeral.

sentences.zh: 」喪家設薦席於喪寢之東，從臨內命婦哭位於其下，主喪以下哭位於喪寢之西，主婦以下哭位於喪寢之北幔下。

translations.literal: " The bereaved family set offering mats east of the mourning chamber; accompanying inner-palace titled ladies' wailing positions were below them; those in charge of mourning and below had wailing positions west of the mourning chamber; the mistress of the house and below had wailing positions beneath the north curtain of the mourning chamber.
translations.idiomatic: " The mourning house set mats east of the death chamber; accompanying ladies wailed below; chief mourners wailed west; the mistress and other women wailed under the north curtain.

sentences.zh: 至日，內使監進堊車，備儀仗導引。

translations.literal: On the day, the eunuch director presented the lime-white carriage and prepared insignia and ushers as guides.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day the eunuch director brought the white funeral carriage with full escort.

sentences.zh: 皇后素服出宮，升輿，三面白布行帷。

translations.literal: The empress in plain dress left the palace, mounted the palanquin, with white cloth traveling screens on three sides.
translations.idiomatic: The empress left in plain dress by palanquin, screened on three sides with white cloth.

sentences.zh: 至閣外，降輿，升堊車。

translations.literal: Reaching outside the gate pavilion, she descended from the palanquin and mounted the lime-white carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the gate pavilion she changed from palanquin to the white funeral carriage.

sentences.zh: 至喪家大門內，降車哭入，仍以行帷圍護。

translations.literal: Reaching inside the great gate of the bereaved family, she descended from the carriage and entered wailing, still screened by the traveling curtains.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the mourning house gate she descended, entered wailing, still screened by the curtains.

sentences.zh: 從臨者皆哭入。

translations.literal: All who accompanied to attend entered wailing.
translations.idiomatic: All attendants entered wailing.

sentences.zh: 喪主以下，降詣西階下立哭。

translations.literal: The chief mourner and those below descended to stand and wail below the west steps.
translations.idiomatic: The chief mourner and others descended to wail below the west steps.

sentences.zh: 皇后升自東階，進至屍東，憑屍哭。

translations.literal: The empress ascended by the east steps, advanced to the east of the corpse, leaned upon the corpse and wailed.
translations.idiomatic: The empress ascended the east steps, reached the corpse's east side, and wailed leaning upon it.

sentences.zh: 從臨者皆哭。

translations.literal: All who accompanied wailed.
translations.idiomatic: All attendants wailed.

sentences.zh: 喪主升自西階，俱哭於屍西。

translations.literal: The chief mourner ascended by the west steps; all wailed west of the corpse.
translations.idiomatic: The chief mourner ascended the west steps; all wailed west of the corpse.

sentences.zh: 皇后至哭位，內使監令跪請止哭。

translations.literal: When the empress reached the wailing position, the eunuch director knelt and requested cessation of wailing.
translations.idiomatic: At the wailing station the eunuch director knelt and asked them to cease wailing.

sentences.zh: 應奉慰者詣皇后前，奉慰如常禮。

translations.literal: Those who should offer consolation went before the empress and offered consolation according to the usual ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Those offering consolation approached the empress by the usual rite.

sentences.zh: 如皇后候成服，則從臨命婦應還者先還。

translations.literal: If the empress waited for completion of mourning dress, then among accompanying titled ladies those who should return returned first.
translations.idiomatic: If the empress stayed for the completion of mourning dress, accompanying ladies who were to return did so first.

sentences.zh: 如本日未即奔喪，則是晡復哭於別殿。

translations.literal: If on that day she did not immediately rush to the bereavement, then at the evening hour they wailed again in the separate hall.
translations.idiomatic: If she did not rush to the funeral that day, wailing resumed at the separate hall in the late afternoon.

sentences.zh: 尚服制皇后齊衰及從臨命婦孝服，俟喪家成服日進之。

translations.literal: The Directorate of Imperial Apparel made the empress's qi mourning and the accompanying titled ladies' mourning garments, to be delivered on the day the bereaved family completed mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Apparel prepared the empress's qi mourning and the ladies' mourning dress, delivered when the mourning house completed its mourning garments.

sentences.zh: 詣靈前再拜，上香，復位，再拜。

translations.literal: They went before the spirit seat, bowed twice, offered incense, returned to position, and bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: Before the spirit seat they bowed twice, offered incense, returned, and bowed again.

sentences.zh: 如爲諸王外戚舉哀，仍於別殿南向，不設薦位。

translations.literal: If raising lamentation for princes' in-laws, it was still in the separate hall facing south, without setting offering positions.
translations.idiomatic: Lamentation for princely in-laws used the separate hall facing south, without offering mats.

sentences.zh: ○遣使臨吊儀

translations.literal: ○ Protocol for dispatching envoys to attend and offer condolences
translations.idiomatic: ○ On dispatching envoys to offer condolences

sentences.zh: 太常司奉旨遣吊。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices received the decree and dispatched condolences.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices dispatched condolence envoys by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 前期，設宣制位於喪家正廳之北，南向；

translations.literal: In advance, the edict-proclamation position was set north of the bereaved family's central hall, facing south;
translations.idiomatic: Beforehand the edict station was placed north of the central hall, facing south;

sentences.zh: 喪主受吊位於南，北向；

translations.literal: the chief mourner's position for receiving condolences was south, facing north;
translations.idiomatic: the chief mourner's reception station was south, facing north;

sentences.zh: 婦人立哭位於殯北幕下。

translations.literal: women standing wailing positions were beneath the curtain north of the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: women's wailing stations stood beneath the curtain north of the coffin.

sentences.zh: 其日，使者至。

translations.literal: On that day the envoy arrived.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day the envoy arrived.

sentences.zh: 喪主去杖，免絰衰服，止哭，出迎於中門外。

translations.literal: The chief mourner put aside the staff, removed the hemp headband and qi mourning, ceased wailing, and went out to receive at the middle gate outside.
translations.idiomatic: The chief mourner laid aside staff and mourning bands, ceased wailing, and met the envoy outside the middle gate.

sentences.zh: 復先入，就廳前拜位。

translations.literal: He re-entered first and took the bowing position before the hall.
translations.idiomatic: He re-entered first and took his bowing station before the hall.

sentences.zh: 內外止哭，使者入，就位稱有制。

translations.literal: Inside and outside ceased wailing; the envoy entered, took position, and announced that there was an edict.
translations.idiomatic: Wailing ceased throughout; the envoy entered, took position, and announced, "There is an edict."

sentences.zh: 喪主以下再拜跪。

translations.literal: The chief mourner and those below bowed twice and knelt.
translations.idiomatic: The chief mourner and others bowed twice and knelt.

sentences.zh: 宣制曰；

translations.literal: The edict was proclaimed:
translations.idiomatic: The envoy proclaimed:

sentences.zh: 「皇帝聞某官薨，遣臣某吊。

translations.literal: "Having heard that such-and-such official has died, the emperor sends me, such-and-such minister, to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: "The emperor, learning that Official X has died, sends me to offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 」喪主以下復再拜。

translations.literal: " The chief mourner and those below again bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: " The chief mourner and others bowed twice again.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，內外皆哭。

translations.literal: When the ritual was complete, inside and outside all wailed.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite ended, all within and without resumed wailing.

sentences.zh: 使者出，喪主至中門外，拜送，杖哭而入。

translations.literal: The envoy departed; the chief mourner reached the middle gate outside, bowed in send-off, and entered leaning on the staff and wailing.
translations.idiomatic: As the envoy left, the chief mourner bowed him out at the middle gate, then re-entered with staff, wailing.

sentences.zh: 宮使則稱有令。

translations.literal: A palace envoy instead announced that there was an order.
translations.idiomatic: Palace envoys announced "There is an order" instead.

sentences.zh: 至遣使賻贈及致奠，其儀節亦相仿云。

translations.literal: As for dispatching envoys for funeral gifts and offering sacrifices, the ritual steps were likewise similar.
translations.idiomatic: Envoy missions for funeral gifts and offerings followed much the same procedure.

sentences.zh: 賻贈之典，一品米六十石，麻布六十匹。

translations.literal: The regulation for funeral gifts: first rank received sixty shi of grain and sixty bolts of hemp cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Funeral gifts for first rank were sixty shi of grain and sixty bolts of hemp cloth.

sentences.zh: 二品以五，三品、四品以四，五品、六品以三，公侯則以百。

translations.literal: Second rank by five, third and fourth ranks by four, fifth and sixth ranks by three; dukes and marquises by one hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Second rank received fifty; third and fourth forty; fifth and sixth thirty; dukes and marquises one hundred.

sentences.zh: 永樂後定制，公、侯、駙馬、伯皆取上裁。

translations.literal: After Yongle the regulation was fixed: dukes, marquises, imperial sons-in-law, and earls all took the upper limit.
translations.idiomatic: After Yongle dukes, marquises, imperial sons-in-law, and earls received the top allowance.

sentences.zh: 凡陣亡者全支，邊遠守禦出征及出海運糧病故半支。

translations.literal: In general those who died in battle received the full allotment; those who died of illness while garrisoning distant frontiers, campaigning, or transporting grain by sea received half.
translations.idiomatic: Battle deaths received full payment; illness deaths on frontier garrison, campaign, or sea grain transport received half.

sentences.zh: 其遣百官會王公大臣喪儀。

translations.literal: As for the protocol for dispatching officials to attend the funerals of princes and great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Protocol for dispatching officials to princes' and senior ministers' funerals.

sentences.zh: 前期，有司於喪家設位次。

translations.literal: In advance, the responsible officials set seat positions at the bereaved family.
translations.idiomatic: Beforehand officials arranged seating at the mourning house.

sentences.zh: 其日，百官應會弔者素服至。

translations.literal: On that day, officials who should attend to offer condolences arrived in plain dress.
translations.idiomatic: On the day attending officials arrived in plain dress.

sentences.zh: 喪主以下就東階哭位，主婦以下就殯北哭位。

translations.literal: The chief mourner and those below took wailing positions at the east steps; the mistress of the house and those below took wailing positions north of the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: The chief mourner wailed at the east steps; the mistress and women wailed north of the coffin.

sentences.zh: 百官入，就殯前位哭，主喪主婦以下皆哭。

translations.literal: Officials entered, took positions before the coffin and wailed; the chief in charge of mourning, mistress, and those below all wailed.
translations.idiomatic: Officials entered, wailed before the coffin; all mourners wailed.

sentences.zh: 止哭，再拜，主喪以下答拜。

translations.literal: Wailing ceased; they bowed twice; those in charge of mourning and below returned the bow.
translations.idiomatic: Wailing ceased; they bowed twice; mourners returned the bows.

sentences.zh: 班首詣喪主前展慰畢，百官出，喪主拜送，杖哭而入。

translations.literal: The ranking head went before the chief mourner and finished offering extended consolation; officials departed; the chief mourner bowed in send-off, leaning on the staff and wailing as he entered.
translations.idiomatic: The lead official offered condolences; officials departed; the chief mourner bowed them out and re-entered wailing with staff.

sentences.zh: 會葬儀同。

translations.literal: The protocol for attending burial was the same.
translations.idiomatic: Burial attendance followed the same rite.

sentences.zh: ○遣使冊贈王公大臣儀

translations.literal: ○ Protocol for dispatching envoys to confer posthumous enfeoffment on princes and great ministers
translations.idiomatic: ○ On dispatching envoys to posthumously enfeoff princes and senior ministers

sentences.zh: 前期，禮部奏請制冊，翰林院取旨制文，中書省禮部奏請某官爲使。

translations.literal: In advance, the Ministry of Rites memorialized requesting preparation of the edict and patent; the Hanlin Academy received the decree and drafted the text; the Secretariat and Ministry of Rites memorialized requesting such-and-such official as envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Beforehand Rites memorialized for the patent, Hanlin drafted the text by decree, and the Secretariat and Rites nominated an envoy.

sentences.zh: 其日，祠祭司設龍亭、香亭於午門前正中，執事於受冊者家設宣制官位於正廳之東北，南向；

translations.literal: On that day the Sacrificial Administration set dragon and incense pavilions at the center before the Meridian Gate; attendants at the patent-recipient's home set the edict-proclamation officer's position northeast of the central hall, facing south;
translations.idiomatic: That day Sacrificial Administration placed dragon and incense pavilions before the Meridian Gate; at the recipient's home attendants placed the edict station northeast of the central hall, facing south;

sentences.zh: 喪主代受冊命者位於廳前，北向。

translations.literal: the chief mourner standing in for the patent recipient was before the hall, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: the chief mourner representing the recipient stood before the hall, facing north.

sentences.zh: 禮部官封冊文，以盝匣盛之，黃袱裹置龍亭中。

translations.literal: A Ministry of Rites officer sealed the patent text, placed it in a lacquer case wrapped in yellow cloth, and set it in the dragon pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: A Rites officer sealed the patent in a lacquer case wrapped in yellow cloth and placed it in the dragon pavilion.

sentences.zh: 儀仗、鼓樂前導，至其家。

translations.literal: Insignia and drum music led the way to the family home.
translations.idiomatic: Insignia and music escorted the party to the home.

sentences.zh: 代受冊者出迎於大門外。

translations.literal: The one standing in to receive the patent went out to receive at the great gate outside.
translations.idiomatic: The representative met them outside the great gate.

sentences.zh: 執事舁龍亭置廳上正中，使者入，立於東北。

translations.literal: Attendants carried the dragon pavilion and set it at the center atop the hall; the envoy entered and stood northeast.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants placed the dragon pavilion at the hall's center; the envoy entered and stood to the northeast.
