sentences.zh: 代受冊者就拜位，再拜。

translations.literal: The stand-in for the patent recipient took the bowing position and bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The representative took the bowing station and bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 使者稍前，稱「有制」。

translations.literal: The envoy stepped slightly forward and announced "There is an edict."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy stepped forward and announced, "There is an edict."

sentences.zh: 代受冊者跪。

translations.literal: The stand-in knelt.
translations.idiomatic: The representative knelt.

sentences.zh: 宣制曰：「皇帝遣臣某，冊贈故某官某爲某勳某爵。

translations.literal: The edict was proclaimed: "The emperor sends me, such-and-such minister, to confer by patent posthumously upon the late such-and-such official such-and-such with such-and-such merit and such-and-such rank.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy proclaimed: "The emperor sends me to posthumously enfeoff the late Official X with such merit and such rank.

sentences.zh: 」宣訖，代受冊者復再拜。

translations.literal: " When the proclamation was finished, the stand-in again bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: " When the proclamation ended, the representative bowed twice again.

sentences.zh: 使者取冊授之，代受冊者捧置靈座前。

translations.literal: The envoy took the patent and handed it over; the stand-in received it with both hands and placed it before the spirit seat.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy handed over the patent; the representative placed it before the spirit seat.

sentences.zh: 使者出，代受冊者送至大門外。

translations.literal: The envoy departed; the stand-in escorted to the great gate outside.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy departed; the representative escorted him to the outer gate.

sentences.zh: 如不用冊者，吏部用誥命，喪家以冊文錄黃，設祭儀於靈前。

translations.literal: If no patent was used, the Ministry of Personnel used a commission of appointment; the bereaved family copied the patent text in yellow and set sacrificial ritual before the spirit seat.
translations.idiomatic: Without a patent, Personnel issued a commission; the mourning house copied the text in yellow and set sacrifice before the spirit seat.

sentences.zh: 代受冊者再拜，執事者展黃立讀於左。

translations.literal: The stand-in bowed twice; attendants unfolded the yellow copy and stood reading it on the left.
translations.idiomatic: The representative bowed twice; attendants unfolded the yellow copy and read it standing to the left.

sentences.zh: 喪主以下皆再拜，焚黃。

translations.literal: The chief mourner and those below all bowed twice and burned the yellow copy.
translations.idiomatic: All mourners bowed twice and burned the yellow copy.

sentences.zh: ○賜祭葬

translations.literal: ○ Bestowal of sacrificial offerings and burial
translations.idiomatic: ○ On grants for sacrifice and burial

sentences.zh: 洪武十四年九月，衍聖公孔希學卒，遣官致祭。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourteenth year of Hongwu, the Duke Who Spread the Sage's Teachings Kong Xixue died; officials were dispatched to offer sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 14, ninth month, Kong Xixue, Duke Who Spread the Sage's Teachings, died; officials were sent to sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 其後，羣臣祭葬，皆有定制。

translations.literal: Thereafter, sacrifice and burial for the host of ministers all had fixed regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter ministers' sacrificial and burial grants were fixed by regulation.

sentences.zh: 太祖諭祭羣臣文，多出御筆。

translations.literal: Taizu's instruction texts for sacrificing to ministers mostly came from the imperial brush.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu's sacrificial texts for ministers were mostly in his own hand.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，世宗爲禮部尚書席書、兵部尚書李承勳親制祭文。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing period, Shizong personally composed sacrificial texts for Minister of Rites Xi Shu and Minister of War Li Chengxun.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing the emperor personally wrote sacrificial texts for Xi Shu and Li Chengxun.

sentences.zh: 皆特典，非常制也。

translations.literal: All were special grants, not ordinary regulations.
translations.idiomatic: These were special favors, not standard practice.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年十二月，禮部議上卹典條例：凡官員祭葬，有無隆殺之等，悉遵《會典》。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Longqing, the Ministry of Rites submitted for discussion relief regulations: for all officials' sacrifice and burial, whether elevated or reduced in grade, all followed the 《Collected Statutes》.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing year 1, twelfth month, Rites proposed relief regulations: all graded sacrificial and burial grants followed the 《Collected Statutes》.

sentences.zh: 其特恩，如侍從必日侍講讀、軍功必躬履行陣、東宮官必出閣講授有勞者。

translations.literal: Special grace applied to such cases as daily attendants who must daily attend lecturing and reading, military merit requiring personal entry into battle ranks, and Eastern Palace officials who had labored in lecturing after leaving the pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Special grace applied to daily lecturing attendants, soldiers with personal battlefield merit, and Eastern Palace tutors who had labored in lecturing.

sentences.zh: 據嘉靖中事例，祭葬加一等，無祭者與祭一罈，無葬者給半葬，半葬者給全葬。

translations.literal: According to Jiajing precedents, sacrifice and burial were raised one grade; those without sacrifice received one altar set; those without burial received half burial; those with half burial received full burial.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing precedents raised grants one grade; those without sacrifice received one altar set; those without burial received half burial; half burial could be raised to full.

sentences.zh: 講讀官五品本身有祭，四品及父母，三品及妻。

translations.literal: Lecturing-and-reading officials of fifth rank received sacrifice for themselves; of fourth rank for parents as well; of third rank for the wife as well.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth-rank lecturers received personal sacrifice; fourth rank added parents; third rank added the wife.

sentences.zh: 軍功四品得祭葬，三品未滿及父母。

translations.literal: Military merit at fourth rank received sacrifice and burial; at third rank if not yet having completed tenure, and for parents.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth-rank military merit earned sacrifice and burial; third-rank officers before completing tenure, and their parents, also qualified.

sentences.zh: 講讀年久、啓沃功多、軍旅身殲、勳勞茂著者，恩恤加厚，臨期請旨。

translations.literal: Lecturers of long years, those with much nourishing counsel, those who perished in military campaigns, and those with outstanding merit and labor received thicker grace and relief; when the time came they requested the decree.
translations.idiomatic: Long-serving lecturers, counselors of great service, soldiers killed in campaign, and men of outstanding merit received enhanced grants by special decree at the time.

sentences.zh: 《會典》，凡一品官，祭九壇。

translations.literal: The 《Collected Statutes》: for all first-rank officials, nine altar sets for sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Collected Statutes》 fixed nine altar sets for first-rank officials.

sentences.zh: 父母妻加祭。

translations.literal: For parents and wife, additional sacrifice was added.
translations.idiomatic: Parents and wives received additional sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 或二壇、一罈，或妻止一罈者，恩難預擬，遇有陳乞，酌擬上請。

translations.literal: Whether two altar sets, one altar set, or the wife receiving only one altar set—the grace was hard to predetermine; when petitions were submitted, discretion was exercised and submission made to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Whether two sets, one set, or a wife receiving only one—the grace could not be fixed in advance; petitions were judged and referred upward.

sentences.zh: 二品，二壇。

translations.literal: Second rank, two altar sets.
translations.idiomatic: Second rank received two altar sets.

sentences.zh: 加東宮三少，或兼大學士贈一品者，至四壇，父母妻俱一罈，致仕加三少者加一罈，加太子太保者加三壇，妻未封夫人者不祭。

translations.literal: With addition of the Three Minor Tutors of the Eastern Palace, or concurrent Grand Secretary enfeoffed posthumously as first rank, up to four altar sets; parents and wife each one altar set; retired officials with added Three Minor Tutors received one additional altar set; those with added Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent received three additional altar sets; if the wife had not been enfeoffed as lady, no sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: With Eastern Palace minor tutorship or posthumous first rank as Grand Secretary, up to four sets; parents and wife each one; retired minor tutors gained one set; Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent gained three; wives not enfeoffed as ladies received no sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 三品祭葬，在任、致仕俱一罈，兼學士贈尚書者二壇，未及考滿病故者一罈減半。

translations.literal: Third-rank sacrifice and burial: whether in office or retired, one altar set each; concurrent academician enfeoffed posthumously as minister of a board received two altar sets; those who died of illness before completing tenure review had one altar set halved.
translations.idiomatic: Third rank received one altar set in or out of office; posthumous ministerial enfeoffment as academician doubled it; death before completing tenure halved the set.

sentences.zh: 造葬悉如舊例。

translations.literal: Provision of burial all followed former precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Burial provisions followed previous precedent.

sentences.zh: 四、五品官不得重封。

translations.literal: Officials of fourth and fifth rank could not receive duplicate enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth- and fifth-rank officials could not receive duplicate enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 故四品官由六七品升者，父母有祭。

translations.literal: Therefore fourth-rank officials promoted from sixth or seventh rank, their parents received sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth-rank officials promoted from sixth or seventh rank secured sacrifice for parents.

sentences.zh: 由五品升者，以例不重封，遂不得祭。

translations.literal: Those promoted from fifth rank, because by precedent there was no duplicate enfeoffment, consequently received no sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Those promoted from fifth rank, barred from duplicate enfeoffment, received no sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 今定四品官，凡經考滿者，父母雖止授五品封，亦與祭一罈。

translations.literal: Now it is fixed: for fourth-rank officials, all who had passed tenure review, even if parents received only fifth-rank enfeoffment, still received one altar set of sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: It was now fixed that fourth-rank officials who completed tenure review secured one altar set for parents even if parents held only fifth-rank enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 四品以上官，本身及父母恩典，必由考滿而後得。

translations.literal: For officials fourth rank and above, grace for themselves and parents had to come after completing tenure review.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth rank and above required completed tenure review before personal or parental grants.

sentences.zh: 然有二品、三品共歷四五年，父母未授三品封，終不得沾一祭者，宜並敘年資。

translations.literal: Yet there were cases of second- and third-rank officials serving four or five years combined while parents received no third-rank enfeoffment and ultimately received not even one sacrifice; seniority in years should also be counted.
translations.idiomatic: Yet some second- and third-rank officials served four or five years combined while parents never received third-rank enfeoffment and gained no sacrifice; years of service should count as well.

sentences.zh: 二品、三品共歷三年以上者，雖未考三品滿，本身及父母俱與三品祭葬。

translations.literal: Second- and third-rank officials with combined service of three years or more, even if third-rank tenure review was not yet complete, themselves and parents all received third-rank sacrifice and burial.
translations.idiomatic: Second- and third-rank officials with three or more combined years of service received third-rank sacrifice and burial for themselves and parents even before completing third-rank tenure review.

sentences.zh: 三品四品，共歷三年以上者，雖未考四品滿，本身用三品未考滿例，祭一罈半，葬父母祭一罈。

translations.literal: Third- and fourth-rank officials with combined service of three years or more, even if fourth-rank tenure review was not yet complete, for themselves applied the precedent for third-rank officials before completing tenure review: one and a half altars for sacrifice; for burying parents, one altar for sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Third- and fourth-rank officials with three or more combined years of service, even before completing fourth-rank tenure review, received for themselves the third-rank precedent for incomplete review—one and a half sacrifice altars—and one altar for burying their parents.

sentences.zh: 凡被劾閒住者，雖遇覃恩，復致仕，仍不給祭葬。

translations.literal: All who were impeached and suspended from office, even if they encountered a broad grace and returned to retirement, still were not granted sacrifice and burial.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone impeached and idled at home was denied sacrifice and burial honors even after a general amnesty or return to retirement.

sentences.zh: 勳臣祭葬，皇親出自上裁。

translations.literal: Sacrifice and burial for meritorious officials; for imperial relatives, the decision came from the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Meritorious officials received regulated sacrifice and burial grants, but imperial kinsmen depended on the throne's personal decision.

sentences.zh: 駙馬都尉祭十五壇。

translations.literal: Imperial sons-in-law, Commandants of the Riding Assistants, received fifteen altars for sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Sons-in-law of the emperor holding the title Commandant of the Riding Assistants were granted fifteen sacrifice altars.

sentences.zh: 公、侯、伯在內掌府事坐營、在外總兵有殊勳加太子太保以上者，遵《會典》。

translations.literal: Dukes, marquises, and earls who within the capital managed princely establishments and commanded camp garrisons, or who outside commanded troops and had extraordinary merit with addition to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent or above, followed the 《Collected Statutes》.
translations.idiomatic: Dukes, marquises, and earls who managed princely establishments in the capital, commanded camp garrisons, or held field command with extraordinary merit and ranks from Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent upward followed the 《Collected Statutes》.

sentences.zh: 公、侯十六壇，伯十五壇，掌府坐營總兵有勳勞者七罈，掌府坐營年勞者五壇，掌府坐營而政跡未著者四壇，管事而被劾勘明閒住者二壇，被劾未經勘實者一罈。

translations.literal: Dukes and marquises sixteen altars, earls fifteen altars; those managing establishments and commanding camp garrisons or field armies with meritorious service seven altars; those managing establishments and commanding camp garrisons with years of service five altars; those managing establishments and commanding camp garrisons but whose administrative record was not distinguished four altars; those who managed affairs but were impeached, investigated, and suspended two altars; those impeached but not yet investigated one altar.
translations.idiomatic: Dukes and marquises received sixteen altars and earls fifteen; commanders of establishments or camps with distinguished merit received seven; those with long service received five; those without notable records received four; officials suspended after substantiated impeachment received two; and those impeached but not yet verified received one.

sentences.zh: 勘實罪重者，並本爵應得祭葬皆削。

translations.literal: When investigation verified serious guilt, all sacrifice and burial due under their original rank were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: If investigation confirmed serious wrongdoing, even the sacrifice and burial honors due their original rank were stripped away.

sentences.zh: 又正德間，公、侯、伯本祭俱三壇，嘉靖間二壇。

translations.literal: Moreover, during the Zhengde reign dukes, marquises, and earls all received three altars for their own sacrifice; during the Jiajing reign, two altars.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhengde emperor, dukes, marquises, and earls each received three personal sacrifice altars; under the Jiajing emperor, only two.

sentences.zh: 今遵嘉靖例，以復《會典》之舊。

translations.literal: At present the Jiajing precedent is followed to restore the former standards of the 《Collected Statutes》.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiajing precedent is now followed to restore the original provisions of the 《Collected Statutes》.

sentences.zh: 武臣祭葬，遵正德、嘉靖例，都督同知僉事、錦衣衛指揮祭三壇，署都督同知僉事一罈，餘推類行之。

translations.literal: Sacrifice and burial for military officials followed the Zhengde and Jiajing precedents: Vice Commissioners-in-chief of the Chief Military Commission and Commanders of the Embroidered Uniform Guard received three altars for sacrifice; Acting Vice Commissioners-in-chief one altar; the remainder were applied by analogy.
translations.idiomatic: Military officials' sacrifice and burial followed Zhengde and Jiajing practice: Vice Commissioners-in-chief and Embroidered Uniform Guard commanders received three altars, acting vice commissioners one altar, and lower ranks by analogy.

sentences.zh: 帝從其議。

translations.literal: The emperor approved their proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted the recommendation.

sentences.zh: 萬曆六年更定，凡致仕養病終養聽用等官，祭葬俱與現任官同。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Wanli it was revised: all officials who had retired, taken leave for illness, returned home for parental care, or awaited appointment received sacrifice and burial equal to incumbent officials.
translations.idiomatic: Revised in Wanli 6, retired officials, those on sick leave, those home on filial care, and those awaiting appointment all received the same sacrifice and burial as active officials.

sentences.zh: 十二年續定，被劾自陳致仕官，有日久論定原無可議者，仍給祭葬，父母妻視本身爲差等。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year it was further fixed: impeached officials who had petitioned to retire, and after long time deliberation were originally found without reproach, still received sacrifice and burial; parents and wives were graded according to the official himself.
translations.idiomatic: Further fixed in Wanli 12, impeached officials who retired on their own petition and were eventually cleared after long review still received sacrifice and burial, with parents and wives ranked one grade below the official.

sentences.zh: ○喪葬之制

translations.literal: ○ Regulations for mourning and burial
translations.idiomatic: ○ On funeral and burial regulations

sentences.zh: 洪武五年定。

translations.literal: Fixed in the fifth year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: These regulations were established in Hongwu 5.

sentences.zh: 凡襲衣，三品以上三，四品、五品二，六品以下一。

translations.literal: For burial garments, third rank and above three, fourth and fifth ranks two, sixth rank and below one.
translations.idiomatic: Burial garments numbered three for third rank and above, two for fourth and fifth ranks, and one for sixth rank and below.

sentences.zh: 飯含，五品以上飯稷含珠，九品以上飯粱含小珠。

translations.literal: For placing grain in the mouth, fifth rank and above placed millet and a pearl; sixth rank and below placed fine grain and a small pearl.
translations.idiomatic: For the mouth-offering rite, fifth rank and above received millet and a pearl; sixth rank and below received fine grain and a small pearl.

sentences.zh: 銘旌、絳帛，廣一幅，四品以上長九尺，六品以上八尺，九品以上七尺。

translations.literal: Memorial pennants and crimson silk were one full width in breadth; fourth rank and above nine feet long, sixth rank and above eight feet, ninth rank and above seven feet.
translations.idiomatic: Memorial pennants and crimson silk were one full width wide: nine feet for fourth rank and above, eight for sixth rank and above, and seven for ninth rank and above.

sentences.zh: 斂衣，品官朝服一襲，常服十襲，衾十番。

translations.literal: Shroud garments: one set of court dress, ten sets of regular dress, and ten layers of quilt.
translations.idiomatic: For the shroud, ranked officials received one court robe, ten everyday robes, and ten quilt layers.

sentences.zh: 靈座設於柩前，作白絹結魂帛以依神。

translations.literal: A spirit seat was set before the coffin, and white silk was fashioned into a soul cloth to lodge the spirit.
translations.idiomatic: A spirit seat was placed before the coffin, with white silk fashioned into a soul cloth to receive the departed spirit.

sentences.zh: 棺槨，品官棺用油杉硃漆，槨用土杉。

translations.literal: Coffin and outer coffin: ranked officials' coffins used oil-treated fir with cinnabar lacquer; outer coffins used local fir.
translations.idiomatic: Ranked officials' coffins were of oil-treated fir lacquered vermilion; outer coffins were of local fir.

sentences.zh: 牆翣，公、侯六，三品以上四，五品以上二。

translations.literal: Wall feather-banners: dukes and marquises six, third rank and above four, fifth rank and above two.
translations.idiomatic: Wall feather-banners numbered six for dukes and marquises, four for third rank and above, and two for fifth rank and above.

sentences.zh: 明器，公、侯九十事，一品、二品八十事，三品、四品七十事，五品六十事，六品、七品三十事，八品、九品二十事。

translations.literal: Spirit objects: dukes and marquises ninety pieces, first and second ranks eighty, third and fourth ranks seventy, fifth rank sixty, sixth and seventh ranks thirty, eighth and ninth ranks twenty.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit objects numbered ninety for dukes and marquises, eighty for first and second ranks, seventy for third and fourth, sixty for fifth, thirty for sixth and seventh, and twenty for eighth and ninth.

sentences.zh: 引者，引車之紼也；

translations.literal: Guides were the cords for drawing the hearse;
translations.idiomatic: Guides were the cords used to draw the funeral carriage;

sentences.zh: 披者，以纁爲之，擊於輀車四柱，在旁執之，以備傾覆者也；

translations.literal: Supports were made of scarlet silk, tied to the four posts of the bier carriage; attendants at the sides held them to guard against overturning;
translations.idiomatic: Supports were scarlet silk ropes tied to the bier carriage's four posts; attendants held them at the sides to prevent the carriage from tipping;

sentences.zh: 鐸者，以銅爲之，所以節輓歌者。

translations.literal: Bells were made of bronze and used to mark the tempo of the dirge.
translations.idiomatic: Bells of bronze marked the tempo of the funeral dirge.

sentences.zh: 公、侯四引六披，左右各八鐸。

translations.literal: Dukes and marquises had four guides and six supports, with eight bells on each side.
translations.idiomatic: Dukes and marquises received four guides and six supports, with eight bells on each side.

sentences.zh: 一品、二品三引四披，左右各六鐸。

translations.literal: First and second ranks had three guides and four supports, with six bells on each side.
translations.idiomatic: First- and second-rank officials had three guides and four supports, with six bells on each side.

sentences.zh: 三品、四品二引二披，左右各四鐸。

translations.literal: Third and fourth ranks had two guides and two supports, with four bells on each side.
translations.idiomatic: Third- and fourth-rank officials had two guides and two supports, with four bells on each side.

sentences.zh: 五品以下，二引二披，左右各二鐸。

translations.literal: Fifth rank and below had two guides and two supports, with two bells on each side.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of fifth rank and below had two guides and two supports, with two bells on each side.

sentences.zh: 羽幡竿長九尺，五品以上，一人執之以引柩，六品以下不用。

translations.literal: Feather banner poles were nine feet long; fifth rank and above had one person carry them to lead the coffin; sixth rank and below did not use them.
translations.idiomatic: Feather banner poles were nine feet long; fifth rank and above used one bearer to lead the coffin, but sixth rank and below did not.

sentences.zh: 功布，品官用之，長三尺。

translations.literal: Merit cloth was used by ranked officials and was three feet long.
translations.idiomatic: Ranked officials used merit cloth three feet in length.

sentences.zh: 方相，四品以上四目，七品以上兩目，八品以下不用。

translations.literal: Exorcist figures: fourth rank and above had four eyes, seventh rank and above two eyes; eighth rank and below did not use them.
translations.idiomatic: Exorcist figures had four eyes for fourth rank and above and two eyes for seventh rank and above; eighth rank and below had none.

sentences.zh: 柳車上用竹格，以彩結之，旁施帷幔，四角重流蘇。

translations.literal: On the willow bier a bamboo frame was used, bound with colored silk; curtains were hung at the sides, and heavy tassels hung at the four corners.
translations.idiomatic: The willow bier bore a bamboo frame bound with colored silk, side curtains, and heavy tassels at each corner.

sentences.zh: 志石二片，品官皆用之。

translations.literal: Two tomb inscription stones were used by all ranked officials.
translations.idiomatic: All ranked officials used two tomb inscription stones.

sentences.zh: 其一爲蓋，書某官之墓；

translations.literal: One served as the lid and bore the inscription "Tomb of such-and-such official";
translations.idiomatic: One served as the cover stone and bore the inscription "Tomb of [title and name]";

sentences.zh: 其一爲底，書姓名、鄉里、三代、生年、卒葬月日及子孫、葬地。

translations.literal: One served as the base and bore the name, native place, three generations, birth year, death and burial dates, descendants, and burial site.
translations.idiomatic: The other served as the base stone and recorded name, native place, three generations, birth and death dates, descendants, and burial location.

sentences.zh: 婦人則隨夫與子孫封贈。

translations.literal: For women, the enfeoffment conferred on husband and descendants was followed.
translations.idiomatic: For women, inscriptions followed the titles conferred on the husband and descendants.

sentences.zh: 二石相向，鐵束埋墓中。

translations.literal: The two stones faced each other and were bound with iron and buried in the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: The two stones faced each other, were bound with iron bands, and buried within the tomb.

sentences.zh: 祭物，四品以上羊豕，九品以上豕。

translations.literal: Sacrificial offerings: fourth rank and above received a sheep and a pig; ninth rank and above a pig.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial offerings included a sheep and pig for fourth rank and above, and a pig alone for ninth rank and above.

sentences.zh: 初，洪武二年，敕葬開平王常遇春於鐘山之陰，給明器九十事，納之墓中。

translations.literal: At the beginning, in the second year of Hongwu, an edict ordered the burial of Prince of Kaiping Chang Yuchun on the northern slope of Bell Mountain, granting ninety spirit objects to be placed in the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, in Hongwu 2, the emperor ordered Prince of Kaiping Chang Yuchun buried on the north slope of Bell Mountain and granted ninety spirit objects for placement in the tomb.

sentences.zh: 鉦二，鼓四，紅旗，拂子各二，紅羅蓋、鞍、籠各一，弓二，箭三，竈、釜、火爐各一，俱以木爲之。

translations.literal: Two gongs, four drums, two red banners, two whisk-brooms each; one red silk canopy, saddle, and cage each; two bows, three arrows; one stove, cauldron, and brazier each—all made of wood.
translations.idiomatic: Two gongs, four drums, two red banners, and two whisk-brooms; one red silk canopy, saddle, and cage; two bows and three arrows; and one stove, cauldron, and brazier apiece—all of wood.

sentences.zh: 水罐、甲、頭盔、臺盞、杓、壺、瓶、酒甕、唾壺、水盆、香爐各一，燭臺二，香盒、香匙各一，香箸二，香匙箸瓶、茶鍾、茶盞各一，箸二，匙二，匙箸瓶一，碗二，楪十二，橐二，俱以錫造，金裹之。

translations.literal: One water jar, suit of armor, helmet, goblet stand, ladle, ewer, vase, wine jar, spittoon, basin, and incense burner each; two candle stands; one incense box and incense spoon each; two incense chopsticks; one incense spoon-and-chopstick vase, tea bell, and tea cup each; two chopsticks; two spoons; one spoon-and-chopstick vase; two bowls; twelve dishes; two pouches—all made of tin and wrapped in gold.
translations.idiomatic: One each of water jar, armor, helmet, goblet stand, ladle, ewer, vase, wine jar, spittoon, basin, and incense burner; two candle stands; one incense box and spoon; two incense chopsticks; one spoon-and-chopstick vase, tea bell, and tea cup; two chopsticks and two spoons; one spoon-and-chopstick vase; two bowls; twelve dishes; and two pouches—all tin wrapped in gold.

sentences.zh: 班劍、牙仗各一，金裹立瓜、骨朵戟、響節各二，交椅、腳踏、馬杌各一，誕馬六，槍、劍、斧、弩、食桌、牀、屏風、柱杖、箱、交牀、香桌各一，凳二，俱以木爲之。

translations.literal: One court sword and ivory staff each; two gold-wrapped standing melons, bone-club halberds, and sounding staves each; one folding chair, footrest, and horse stool each; six ceremonial horses; one spear, sword, axe, crossbow, dining table, bed, screen, walking stick, chest, folding bed, and incense table each; two stools—all made of wood.
translations.idiomatic: One court sword and ivory staff; two gold-wrapped standing melons, bone-club halberds, and sounding staves; one folding chair, footrest, and horse stool; six ceremonial horses; and one spear, sword, axe, crossbow, dining table, bed, screen, walking stick, chest, folding bed, and incense table; plus two stools—all of wood.

sentences.zh: 樂工十六，執儀伏二十四，控士六，女使十，青龍、白虎、硃雀、玄武神四，門神二，武士十，並以木造，各高一尺。

translations.literal: Sixteen musicians, twenty-four bearers of ritual regalia, six grooms, ten female attendants, four spirit gods of the Azure Dragon, White Tiger, Vermilion Bird, and Black Tortoise, two door gods, and ten warriors—all made of wood, each one foot high.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen musicians, twenty-four ritual attendants, six grooms, ten female attendants, the four directional spirit gods, two door gods, and ten warriors—all wooden figures one foot high.

sentences.zh: 雜物，翣六，璧一，筐、笥、楎、椸、衿、鞶各一，笣二，筲二，糧漿瓶二，油瓶一，紗廚、暖帳各一。

translations.literal: Miscellaneous objects: six feather-banners, one jade disk, one basket, box, clothes rack, pole, collar, and belt each; two bundles; two rice measures; two grain-and-soup bottles; one oil bottle; one gauze kitchen screen and warming canopy each.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous grave goods included six feather-banners, one jade disk, one each of basket, box, clothes rack, pole, collar, and belt; two bundles; two rice measures; two grain-and-soup bottles; one oil bottle; and one gauze screen and warming canopy.

sentences.zh: 束帛青三段，纁二段，每段長一丈八尺。

translations.literal: Bundled silk: three sections of blue and two sections of scarlet, each section one zhang and eight chi long.
translations.idiomatic: Bundled silk comprised three sections of blue and two of scarlet, each one zhang and eight chi in length.

sentences.zh: 後定制，公、侯九十事者准此行之。

translations.literal: Later when regulations were fixed, dukes and marquises with ninety spirit objects followed this as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: When regulations were later fixed, the ninety spirit objects granted to dukes and marquises became the standard.

sentences.zh: 餘以次減殺。

translations.literal: The remainder were reduced step by step according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: Lower ranks received proportionally reduced allotments.

sentences.zh: ○碑碣

translations.literal: ○ Steles and stelae
translations.idiomatic: ○ On steles and stelae

sentences.zh: 明初，文武大臣薨逝，例請於上，命翰林官制文，立神道碑。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Ming, when civil and military great ministers died, by precedent they petitioned the throne, and the emperor ordered Hanlin officials to compose texts and erect spirit-way steles.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the dynasty, when senior civil and military ministers died, their families petitioned the throne for Hanlin scholars to compose texts and erect spirit-way steles.

sentences.zh: 惟太祖時中山王徐達、成祖時榮國公姚廣孝及弘治中昌國公張巒治先塋，皆出御筆。

translations.literal: Only under Taizu for Prince of Zhongshan Xu Da, under Chengzu for Prince of Rongguo Yao Guangxiao, and under Hongzhi for Duke of Changguo Zhang Luan in tending his ancestral grave—all came from the imperial brush.
translations.idiomatic: Only Xu Da, Prince of Zhongshan under Taizu; Yao Guangxiao, Prince of Rongguo under Chengzu; and Zhang Luan, Duke of Changguo under Hongzhi, who tended his family's grave—all received texts from the emperor's own brush.

sentences.zh: 其制自洪武三年定。

translations.literal: The regulations were first fixed in the third year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: The system was first established in Hongwu 3.

sentences.zh: 五品以上用碑，龜趺螭首。

translations.literal: Fifth rank and above used steles with tortoise pedestals and dragon heads.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of fifth rank and above used steles with tortoise bases and dragon heads.

sentences.zh: 六品以下用碣，方趺圓首。

translations.literal: Sixth rank and below used stelae with square pedestals and round tops.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of sixth rank and below used stelae with square bases and rounded tops.

sentences.zh: 五年，復詳定其制。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, the regulations were again fixed in detail.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the regulations were revised in detail.

sentences.zh: 功臣歿後封王，螭首高三尺二寸，碑身高九尺，廣三尺六寸，龜趺高三尺八寸。

translations.literal: Meritorious officials enfeoffed as kings after death: dragon head three chi two cun high, stele body nine chi high and three chi six cun wide, tortoise pedestal three chi eight cun high.
translations.idiomatic: Meritorious officials posthumously enfeoffed as kings received steles with dragon heads three chi two cun high, bodies nine chi high by three chi six cun wide, and tortoise pedestals three chi eight cun high.

sentences.zh: 一品螭首，二品麟鳳蓋，三品天祿辟邪蓋，四品至七品方趺。

translations.literal: First rank dragon head, second rank qilin-and-phoenix cap, third rank celestial-blessing-and-ward-off-evil cap, fourth through seventh ranks square pedestal.
translations.idiomatic: First rank used dragon heads, second rank qilin-and-phoenix caps, third rank celestial-blessing-and-ward-off-evil caps, and fourth through seventh ranks square pedestals.

sentences.zh: 首視功臣歿後封王者，遞殺二寸，至一尺八寸止。

translations.literal: The cap, taking as standard that for meritorious officials enfeoffed as kings after death, was reduced by two cun at each step down to one chi eight cun.
translations.idiomatic: Cap height, measured from the standard for posthumous royal enfeoffment, decreased by two cun per rank down to one chi eight cun.

sentences.zh: 碑身遞殺五寸，至五尺五寸止。

translations.literal: The stele body was reduced by five cun at each step down to five chi five cun.
translations.idiomatic: Stele body height decreased by five cun per rank down to five chi five cun.

sentences.zh: 其廣遞殺二寸，至二尺二寸止。

translations.literal: Its width was reduced by two cun at each step down to two chi two cun.
translations.idiomatic: Stele width decreased by two cun per rank down to two chi two cun.

sentences.zh: 趺遞殺二寸，至二尺四寸止。

translations.literal: The pedestal was reduced by two cun at each step down to two chi four cun.
translations.idiomatic: Pedestal height decreased by two cun per rank down to two chi four cun.

sentences.zh: 墳塋之制，亦洪武三年定。

translations.literal: Regulations for tombs and grave enclosures were also fixed in the third year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: Tomb and grave-enclosure regulations were likewise established in Hongwu 3.

sentences.zh: 一品，塋地周圍九十步，墳高一丈八尺。

translations.literal: First rank: grave enclosure ninety paces in circumference, mound one zhang eight chi high.
translations.idiomatic: First rank: a grave enclosure ninety paces around and a mound one zhang eight chi high.

sentences.zh: 二品，八十步，高一丈四尺。

translations.literal: Second rank: eighty paces, one zhang four chi high.
translations.idiomatic: Second rank: eighty paces around and one zhang four chi high.

sentences.zh: 三品，七十步，高一丈二尺。

translations.literal: Third rank: seventy paces, one zhang two chi high.
translations.idiomatic: Third rank: seventy paces around and one zhang two chi high.

sentences.zh: 以上石獸各六。

translations.literal: For the above ranks, stone beasts six each.
translations.idiomatic: For these ranks, six stone beasts were permitted.

sentences.zh: 四品，四十步。

translations.literal: Fourth rank: forty paces.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth rank: forty paces around.

sentences.zh: 七品以下二十步，高六尺。

translations.literal: Seventh rank and below twenty paces, six chi high.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh rank and below: twenty paces around and six chi high.

sentences.zh: 五年重定。

translations.literal: Revised in the fifth year.
translations.idiomatic: These measures were revised in the fifth year.

sentences.zh: 功臣歿後封王，塋地周圍一百步，墳高二丈，四圍牆高一丈，石人四，文武各二，石虎、羊、馬、石望柱各二。

translations.literal: Meritorious officials enfeoffed as kings after death: grave enclosure one hundred paces in circumference, mound two zhang high, surrounding wall one zhang high, four stone figures with two civil and two military, two stone tigers, sheep, horses, and stone pillars each.
translations.idiomatic: Meritorious officials posthumously enfeoffed as kings received enclosures one hundred paces around, mounds two zhang high, walls one zhang high, four stone figures (two civil and two military), and two each of stone tigers, sheep, horses, and pillars.

sentences.zh: 一品至六品塋地如舊制，七品加十步。

translations.literal: First through sixth ranks kept the old grave-enclosure measures; seventh rank added ten paces.
translations.idiomatic: First through sixth ranks kept the original enclosure sizes; seventh rank gained ten paces.

sentences.zh: 一品墳高一丈八尺，二品至七品遞殺二尺。

translations.literal: First rank mound one zhang eight chi high; second through seventh ranks reduced by two chi at each step.
translations.idiomatic: First-rank mounds stood one zhang eight chi high; second through seventh ranks decreased by two chi per rank.

sentences.zh: 一品墳牆高九尺，二品至四品遞殺一尺，五品四尺。

translations.literal: First rank grave wall nine chi high; second through fourth ranks reduced by one chi at each step; fifth rank four chi.
translations.idiomatic: First-rank grave walls stood nine chi high; second through fourth ranks decreased by one chi per rank; fifth rank four chi.

sentences.zh: 一品、二品石人二，文武各一，虎、羊、馬、望柱各二。

translations.literal: First and second ranks two stone figures with one civil and one military each; tigers, sheep, horses, and pillars two each.
translations.idiomatic: First and second ranks received two stone figures (one civil, one military) and two each of tigers, sheep, horses, and pillars.

sentences.zh: 三品四品無石人，五品無石虎，六品以下無。

translations.literal: Third and fourth ranks had no stone figures; fifth rank had no stone tigers; sixth rank and below had none.
translations.idiomatic: Third and fourth ranks had no stone figures; fifth rank had no stone tigers; sixth rank and below had none at all.

sentences.zh: 當太祖時，盱眙揚王墳置守戶二百一十，宿州徐王墳置墳戶九十三，滁州滁陽王墳亦置墳戶。

translations.literal: During Taizu's reign, at the tomb of Prince of Yang of Xuyi two hundred and ten tomb-guard households were established; at the tomb of Prince of Xu in Suzhou ninety-three tomb households; at the tomb of Prince of Chuyang in Chuzhou tomb households were also established.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizu, two hundred and ten guard households were assigned to Prince of Yang of Xuyi's tomb, ninety-three to Prince of Xu's tomb at Suzhou, and guard households were also assigned to Prince of Chuyang's tomb at Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，又賜功臣李善長、徐達、常茂、馮勝墳戶百五十，鄧愈、唐勝宗、陸仲亨、華雲龍、顧時、陳德、耿炳文、吳楨、孫恪、郭興墳戶百。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, tomb households of one hundred and fifty were also granted to meritorious officials Li Shanchang, Xu Da, Chang Mao, and Feng Sheng, and one hundred each to Deng Yu, Tang Shengzong, Lu Zhongheng, Hua Yunlong, Gu Shi, Chen De, Geng Bingwen, Wu Zhen, Sun Ke, and Guo Xing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, one hundred and fifty tomb-guard households were granted to Li Shanchang, Xu Da, Chang Mao, and Feng Sheng, and one hundred each to Deng Yu, Tang Shengzong, Lu Zhongheng, Hua Yunlong, Gu Shi, Chen De, Geng Bingwen, Wu Zhen, Sun Ke, and Guo Xing.

sentences.zh: 成化十五年，南京禮部言：「常遇春、李文忠等十四人勳臣墳墓，俱在南京城外，文忠曾孫萼等，以歲久頹壞爲言，請命工修治。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Chenghua, the Nanjing Ministry of Rites said: "The tombs of the fourteen meritorious officials including Chang Yuchun and Li Wenzhong are all outside Nanjing city; Wenzhong's great-grandson E and others, citing long decay, petitioned that craftsmen be ordered to repair them.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 15, the Nanjing Ministry of Rites reported: "The tombs of fourteen meritorious officials including Chang Yuchun and Li Wenzhong lie outside Nanjing; Wenzhong's great-grandson E and others, citing long neglect, asked that craftsmen be sent to restore them.

sentences.zh: 」帝可其奏，且令無子孫者，覆墓旁一人守護之。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved the memorial and also ordered that where there were no descendants, one person from beside the tomb be assigned to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved and ordered that tombs without descendants be assigned one local guardian from nearby.

sentences.zh: ○賜諡

translations.literal: ○ Bestowing posthumous titles
translations.idiomatic: ○ On bestowing posthumous titles

sentences.zh: 親王例用一字；

translations.literal: Princes of the blood by precedent used one character;
translations.idiomatic: Princes of the blood customarily received one-character posthumous titles;

sentences.zh: 郡王二字，文武大臣同。

translations.literal: princes of commanderies two characters, the same as civil and military great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: princes of commanderies two characters, as did senior civil and military ministers.

sentences.zh: 與否自上裁。

translations.literal: Whether granted or not came from the emperor's decision.
translations.idiomatic: Whether a title was granted rested entirely with the throne.

sentences.zh: 若官品未高而侍從有勞，或以死勤事者，特賜諡，非常例。

translations.literal: If rank was not yet high but service in attendance had merit, or if one died diligent in office, a special posthumous title was granted—not the regular precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of modest rank who served the throne faithfully, or who died in the performance of duty, might receive exceptional posthumous titles outside the usual rules.

sentences.zh: 洪武初，有應得諡者，禮部請旨，令禮部行翰林院擬奏。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongwu, when there were those who should receive posthumous titles, the Ministry of Rites petitioned for instruction and ordered the Ministry of Rites to request the Hanlin Academy to draft a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Hongwu, when an official merited a posthumous title, the Ministry of Rites sought imperial instruction and had the Hanlin Academy draft the memorial.

sentences.zh: 弘治十五年定制，凡親王薨，行撫、按，郡王病故，行本府親王及承奉長史，核勘以奏，乃議諡。

translations.literal: Fixed in the fifteenth year of Hongzhi: whenever a prince of the blood died, the provincial surveillance and administration commissioners were dispatched; when a prince of a commandery died of illness, the princely establishment of that commandery and the chief steward were dispatched; investigation was submitted, and only then was the posthumous title deliberated.
translations.idiomatic: Fixed in Hongzhi 15: when a prince of the blood died, provincial officials investigated and reported before a posthumous title was considered; when a commandery prince died, the local princely establishment and chief steward conducted the review.

sentences.zh: 文武大臣請諡，禮部取旨，行吏兵部考實蹟。

translations.literal: When civil and military great ministers petitioned for posthumous titles, the Ministry of Rites sought instruction and dispatched the Ministries of Personnel and War to verify their records.
translations.idiomatic: When senior ministers sought posthumous titles, the Ministry of Rites sought imperial approval and had the Ministries of Personnel and War verify their careers.

sentences.zh: 禮部定三等，行業俱優者爲上，頗可者爲中，行實無取者爲下，送翰林院擬諡。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites fixed three grades: those with conduct and achievement both excellent as upper, those fairly acceptable as middle, and those whose conduct and achievement were worthless as lower, and sent them to the Hanlin Academy to draft posthumous titles.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites ranked candidates in three grades—superior, acceptable, and unworthy—and forwarded them to the Hanlin Academy to draft titles.

sentences.zh: 有應諡而未得者，撫、按、科道官以聞。

translations.literal: Where there were those who should receive posthumous titles but had not yet received them, surveillance, administration, and censorial officials reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial and censorial officials reported cases where a posthumous title was deserved but not yet granted.

sentences.zh: 按明初舊制，諡法自十七字至一字，各有等差。

translations.literal: According to the old system at the beginning of the Ming, posthumous-title law ranged from seventeen characters to one character, each grade having its difference.
translations.idiomatic: Under the early Ming system, posthumous titles ranged from seventeen characters down to one, each rank having its proper measure.

sentences.zh: 然終高帝世，文臣未嘗得諡，武臣非贈侯伯不可得。

translations.literal: Yet throughout Gaodi's reign civil officials never received posthumous titles; military officials could not receive them unless enfeoffed marquis or earl.
translations.idiomatic: Yet throughout Taizu's reign no civil official received a posthumous title, and military officials received them only if posthumously enfeoffed marquis or earl.

sentences.zh: 魯、秦二王曰荒、曰愍。

translations.literal: The two princes of Lu and Qin were titled Huang and Min respectively.
translations.idiomatic: The Princes of Lu and Qin received the posthumous titles Huang ("Reckless") and Min ("Lamented") respectively.

sentences.zh: 至建文諡王禕，成祖諡胡廣，文臣始有諡。

translations.literal: Only when Jianwen posthumously titled Wang Yi and Chengzu posthumously titled Hu Guang did civil officials first receive posthumous titles.
translations.idiomatic: Civil officials first received posthumous titles only when Jianwen titled Wang Yi and Chengzu titled Hu Guang.

sentences.zh: 迨世宗則濫及方士，且加四字矣。

translations.literal: By the Shizong reign they were lavished even on Daoist masters, and four-character titles were added.
translations.idiomatic: By the Jiajing emperor's reign titles were lavished even on Daoist adepts, and four-character epithets appeared.

sentences.zh: 定例，三品得諡，詞臣諡「文」。

translations.literal: By fixed precedent, third rank could receive posthumous titles; literary officials received the character "Wen."
translations.idiomatic: By regulation, third rank qualified for a posthumous title, and literary officials received the character Wen ("Cultured").

sentences.zh: 然亦有得諡不止三品，諡「文。

translations.literal: Yet there were also those who received posthumous titles though not limited to third rank, titled "Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Yet some received posthumous titles below third rank with the character Wen ("Cultured").

sentences.zh: 」不專詞臣者，或以勳勞，或以節義，或以望實，破格崇褒，用示激勸。

translations.literal: "Wen" was not limited to literary officials alone: some for meritorious service, some for integrity and righteousness, some for reputation and achievement—breaking precedent to honor highly, to show encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Such titles were not reserved for literary officials alone: some were granted for merit, some for integrity, some for standing and achievement, as exceptional honors meant to encourage others.

sentences.zh: 其冒濫者，亦間有之。

translations.literal: There were also occasional cases of improper lavish granting.
translations.idiomatic: Improper grants occurred from time to time as well.

sentences.zh: 萬曆元年，禮臣言：「大臣應得諡者，宜廣詢嚴核。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wanli, ritual officials said: "Great ministers who should receive posthumous titles ought to be broadly consulted and strictly verified.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 1, ritual officials argued: "Ministers deserving posthumous titles should be widely consulted and rigorously reviewed.

sentences.zh: 應諡而未請者，不拘遠近，撫、按、科道舉奏，酌議補給。

translations.literal: Those who should receive posthumous titles but had not yet petitioned, without restriction by distance—surveillance commissioners, administration commissioners, and censorial officials memorialized and reported; deliberation was made to supplement grants.
translations.idiomatic: Where a posthumous title was owed but no petition had yet been filed, provincial and censorial officials were to report the case regardless of distance, and the ministry would deliberate on a supplemental grant.

sentences.zh: 」十二年，禮臣言：「大臣諡號，必公論允服，毫無瑕疵者，具請上裁。

translations.literal: " In the twelfth year, ritual officials said: "Posthumous titles for great ministers must go only to those whom public opinion fully accepts, without the slightest blemish; the complete petition was submitted for imperial decision."
translations.idiomatic: " In Wanli 12, ritual officials argued: "A minister's posthumous title should be granted only when public opinion is unanimous and his record is spotless; the full petition should then be submitted for the throne's decision."

sentences.zh: 如行業平常，即官品雖崇，不得概予。

translations.literal: If conduct and achievement were ordinary, even if official rank was lofty, titles could not be granted indiscriminately.
translations.idiomatic: If a man's conduct and career were merely ordinary, he could not receive a title simply because his rank was high.

sentences.zh: 」帝皆從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved all of this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved all of it.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，禮部侍郎郭正域請嚴諡典。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, Vice Minister of Rites Guo Zhengyu petitioned to tighten posthumous-title standards.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 31, Vice Minister of Rites Guo Zhengyu petitioned to enforce the posthumous-title code more strictly.

sentences.zh: 議奪者四人：許論、黃光升、呂本、範廉；

translations.literal: Four whose titles deliberation sought to revoke: Xu Lun, Huang Guangsheng, Lü Ben, and Fan Lian;
translations.idiomatic: Four men whose titles were proposed for revocation: Xu Lun, Huang Guangsheng, Lü Ben, and Fan Lian;

sentences.zh: 應奪而改者一人：陳瓚；

translations.literal: One who should have had his title revoked but had it changed instead: Chen Zan;
translations.idiomatic: one man whose title ought to have been revoked but was altered instead: Chen Zan;

sentences.zh: 補者七人：伍文定、吳悌、魯穆、楊繼宗、鄒智、楊源、陳有年。

translations.literal: Seven to be granted supplemental titles: Wu Wendeng, Wu Ti, Lu Mu, Yang Jizong, Zou Zhi, Yang Yuan, and Chen Younian.
translations.idiomatic: and seven men proposed for supplemental titles: Wu Wendeng, Wu Ti, Lu Mu, Yang Jizong, Zou Zhi, Yang Yuan, and Chen Younian.

sentences.zh: 閣臣沈一貫、硃賡力庇呂本，不從其議。

translations.literal: Grand Secretaries Shen Yiguan and Zhu Geng forcefully shielded Lü Ben and did not follow that deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretaries Shen Yiguan and Zhu Geng vigorously protected Lü Ben, and the court did not adopt the proposal.

sentences.zh: 未幾，御史張邦俊請以呂柟從祀孔廟，而論應補諡者，雍泰、魏學曾等十四人。

translations.literal: Before long, Censor Zhang Bangjun petitioned that Lü Shan be admitted to sacrifices at the Confucian temple, and discussed fourteen who merited supplemental posthumous titles, including Yong Tai and Wei Xuezeng.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, Censor Zhang Bangjun petitioned that Lü Shan be enshrined in the Confucian temple and named fourteen men who deserved supplemental posthumous titles, including Yong Tai and Wei Xuezeng.

sentences.zh: 部議久之，共匯題先後七十四人，留中不發。

translations.literal: After long deliberation at the ministry, seventy-four persons were compiled in memorials in order; the memorials were retained at court and not issued.
translations.idiomatic: After prolonged review, the ministry compiled seventy-four names in successive memorials, but the papers were kept at court and never issued.

sentences.zh: 天啓元年，始降旨俞允，又增續請者十人，而邦俊原請九人不與。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianqi, imperial instruction finally approved; ten additional petitioners were added, but Zhang Bangjun's original nine were not included.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi 1, the throne finally approved the grants, adding ten further petitioners, but the nine men in Zhang Bangjun's original memorial were excluded.

sentences.zh: 正域所請伍文定等亦至是始定。

translations.literal: Wu Wendeng and others whom Zhengyu had petitioned for were also settled only at this time.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Wendeng and the others for whom Zhengyu had petitioned were settled only then.

sentences.zh: 凡八十四人。

translations.literal: In all, eighty-four persons.
translations.idiomatic: In all, eighty-four men received titles.

sentences.zh: 其官卑得諡者，鄒智、劉臺、魏良弼、周天佐、楊允繩、沈煉、楊源、黃鞏、楊慎、周怡、莊鷫、馮應京皆以直諫，孟秋、張元忭、曹端、賀欽、陳茂烈、馬理、陶望齡皆以學行，張銓以忠義，李夢陽以文章，魯穆、楊繼宗、張朝瑞、硃冠、傅新德、張允濟皆以清節，楊慎之文憲，莊鷫之文節，則又兼論文學云。

translations.literal: Among those of low rank who received posthumous titles, Zou Zhi, Liu Tai, Wei Liangbi, Zhou Tianzuo, Yang Yunchang, Shen Lian, Yang Yuan, Huang Gong, Yang Shen, Zhou Yi, Zhuang E, and Feng Yingjing all for direct remonstrance; Meng Qiu, Zhang Yuanbian, Cao Duan, He Qin, Chen Maolie, Ma Li, and Tao Wangling all for learning and conduct; Zhang Quan for loyalty and righteousness; Li Mengyang for literary achievement; Lu Mu, Yang Jizong, Zhang Chaorui, Zhu Guan, Fu Xinde, and Zhang Yunji all for integrity; Yang Shen's Wen Xian and Zhuang E's Wen Jie were additionally granted with literary merit in view.
translations.idiomatic: Among those of modest rank who received posthumous titles, Zou Zhi, Liu Tai, Wei Liangbi, Zhou Tianzuo, Yang Yunchang, Shen Lian, Yang Yuan, Huang Gong, Yang Shen, Zhou Yi, Zhuang E, and Feng Yingjing were honored for forthright remonstrance; Meng Qiu, Zhang Yuanbian, Cao Duan, He Qin, Chen Maolie, Ma Li, and Tao Wangling for scholarship and conduct; Zhang Quan for loyalty; Li Mengyang for literary achievement; Lu Mu, Yang Jizong, Zhang Chaorui, Zhu Guan, Fu Xinde, and Zhang Yunji for moral integrity. Yang Shen's title Wen Xian and Zhuang E's Wen Jie reflected literary merit as well.

sentences.zh: 三年，禮部尚書林堯俞言：「諡典五年一舉，自萬曆四十五年至今，蒙恤而未諡者，九卿臺省會議與臣部酌議。

translations.literal: In the third year, Minister of Rites Lin Yaoyu said: "The posthumous-title rite is held once every five years; from Wanli 45 until now, those who received imperial condolence grants but not posthumous titles—the Nine Ministers and censorial offices should confer with my ministry in deliberation."
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi 3, Minister of Rites Lin Yaoyu said: "Posthumous titles are conferred once every five years. From Wanli 45 until now, officials who received imperial condolence grants but no posthumous title should be reviewed jointly by the Nine Ministers, the censorial offices, and my ministry."

sentences.zh: 」帝可之。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 然是時，遲速無定。

translations.literal: Yet at this time there was no fixed rule for timing.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, there was still no fixed schedule for when titles would be granted.

sentences.zh: 六年，禮科給事中彭汝楠言：「耳目近則睹記真，宜勿逾五年之限。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Supervising Secretary of the Ministry of Rites Peng Runan said: "When one's ears and eyes are near, what one sees and records is true; the five-year limit ought not be exceeded."
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi 6, Supervising Secretary of the Ministry of Rites Peng Runan argued: "When witnesses are still living, the record remains reliable; the five-year limit should not be exceeded."

sentences.zh: 」又謂：「三品以上爲當予諡，而建文諸臣之忠義，陶安等之參帷幄，葉琛等之殉行間，皆宜補諡。

translations.literal: " He also said: "Third rank and above should receive posthumous titles as a matter of course; but the loyalty and righteousness of Jianwen's officials, Tao An and others who took part in strategic planning, Ye Chen and others who died in the ranks—all ought to receive supplemental posthumous titles."
translations.idiomatic: " He also argued that third rank and above should receive posthumous titles as a matter of course, but that the loyal Jianwen officials, Tao An and others who had served in the inner councils, and Ye Chen and others who had died in battle all deserved retroactive titles.

sentences.zh: 」事下禮部，以建文諸臣未易輕擬，不果行。

translations.literal: " The matter was referred to the Ministry of Rites; because Jianwen's officials could not easily be granted titles without careful consideration, it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: " The matter was referred to the Ministry of Rites, but because Jianwen's officials could not be titled lightly, nothing was done.

sentences.zh: 至福王時，始從工科給事中李清言，追諡開國功臣李善長等十四人，正德諫臣蔣欽等十四人，天啓慘死諸臣左光斗等九人，而建文帝之弟允熥、允ＡＲ、允熙，子文奎，亦皆因清疏追補。

translations.literal: Only under the Prince of Fu did the court finally follow Supervising Secretary of the Ministry of Works Li Qing's petition to confer posthumous titles retroactively on fourteen founding ministers including Li Shanchang, fourteen remonstrating officials of the Zhengde reign including Jiang Qin, nine officials of the Tianqi reign who died miserably including Zuo Guangdou; and the Jianwen Emperor's brothers Yun Ti, Yun Qian, and Yun Xi, and his son Wen Kui, were also retroactively granted through memorials petitioning for clarification.
translations.idiomatic: Only under the Prince of Fu did the court finally adopt the proposal of Supervising Secretary of the Ministry of Works Li Qing and confer retroactive posthumous titles on fourteen founding ministers including Li Shanchang, fourteen remonstrating officials of the Zhengde reign including Jiang Qin, and nine Tianqi officials who had died violently, including Zuo Guangdou. The Jianwen Emperor's brothers Yun Ti, Yun Qian, and Yun Xi, and his son Wen Kui, were also granted titles through later clarifying memorials.

sentences.zh: ○品官喪禮

translations.literal: ○ Mourning rites for ranked officials
translations.idiomatic: ○ On mourning rites for ranked officials

sentences.zh: 品官喪禮載在《集禮》、《會典》者，本之《儀禮·士喪》，稽諸《唐典》，又參以硃子《家禮》之編，通行共曉。

translations.literal: Ranked officials' mourning rites recorded in the 《Collected Rites》 and the 《Institutional Compendium》 are based on the 《Rites of Zhou: Mourning for a Gentleman》, checked against Tang codes, and also incorporate Zhu Xi's compilation of the 《Family Rituals》—widely known and understood.
translations.idiomatic: The mourning rites for ranked officials recorded in the 《Collected Rites》 and the 《Institutional Compendium》 derive from the 《Rites of Zhou: Mourning for a Gentleman》, follow Tang precedents, and incorporate Zhu Xi's 《Family Rituals》; they were widely understood throughout the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 茲舉大要，其儀節不具錄。

translations.literal: Here the main points are set forth; the ceremonial details are not fully recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Only the main points are given here; the full ceremonial sequence is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 凡初終之禮，疾病，遷於正寢。

translations.literal: For rites from first illness to death: when ill, move to the main chamber.
translations.idiomatic: For the rites from first illness to death: when illness sets in, the sick person is moved to the main chamber.

sentences.zh: 屬纊，俟絕氣乃哭。

translations.literal: Place the silken wisp; wait until breath is cut off before weeping.
translations.idiomatic: A silken wisp is placed at the mouth; weeping begins only after the last breath.

sentences.zh: 立喪主、主婦，護喪以子孫賢能者。

translations.literal: Establish a chief mourner and mistress of mourning; assign mourning supervision to capable sons and grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: A chief mourner and mistress of mourning are appointed, and capable sons or grandsons are chosen to oversee the funeral.

sentences.zh: 治棺訃告。

translations.literal: Prepare the coffin and death announcement.
translations.idiomatic: The coffin is prepared and death notices are sent out.

sentences.zh: 設必屍牀、帷堂，掘坎。

translations.literal: Set up the corpse couch and curtained hall; dig a pit.
translations.idiomatic: A corpse couch and curtained hall are set up, and a pit is dug.

sentences.zh: 設沐具，沐者四人，六品以下三人，乃含。

translations.literal: Prepare bathing implements; four bathers for fifth rank and above, three for sixth rank and below; then place the mouth-offering.
translations.idiomatic: Bathing implements are prepared; fifth rank and above employ four bathers, sixth rank and below three; then the mouth-offering is placed.

sentences.zh: 置虛座，結魂帛，立銘旌。

translations.literal: Set an empty seat, tie the soul cloth, erect the memorial pennant.
translations.idiomatic: An empty seat is set out, the soul cloth is tied, and the memorial pennant is raised.

sentences.zh: 喪之明日乃小斂，又明日大斂，蓋棺，設靈牀於柩東。

translations.literal: The day after death perform the lesser encoffining; the next day the greater encoffining, cover the coffin, and set the spirit couch east of the bier.
translations.idiomatic: The day after death comes the lesser encoffining; the next day the greater encoffining, the coffin is closed, and a spirit couch is placed east of the bier.

sentences.zh: 又明日，五服之人各服其服，然後朝哭相吊。

translations.literal: Again the next day, persons of the five mourning grades each wear their proper dress, then perform the morning wailing and mutual condolence visits.
translations.idiomatic: On the following day, mourners of every mourning grade don their proper dress and then perform the morning wailing and exchange condolence visits.

sentences.zh: 既成服，朝夕奠，百日而卒哭。

translations.literal: Once mourning dress is complete, offer libations morning and evening; after one hundred days perform the ended wailing.
translations.idiomatic: Once mourning dress is complete, offerings are made morning and evening; after one hundred days the ended wailing is performed.

sentences.zh: 乃擇地，三月而葬。

translations.literal: Then choose the burial site; bury after three months.
translations.idiomatic: A burial site is then chosen, and interment takes place after three months.

sentences.zh: 告后土，遂穿壙。

translations.literal: Announce to the Earth Queen, then excavate the tomb chamber.
translations.idiomatic: The Earth Queen is notified, and the tomb chamber is excavated.

sentences.zh: 刻志石，造明器，備大舉，作神主。

translations.literal: Carve the epitaph stone, prepare burial objects, arrange the full funeral procession, and make the spirit tablet.
translations.idiomatic: The epitaph stone is carved, burial objects are made, the full funeral procession is prepared, and the spirit tablet is fashioned.

sentences.zh: 既發引，至墓所，乃窆。

translations.literal: After the coffin is borne forth, upon reaching the grave, inter the remains.
translations.idiomatic: Once the procession sets out and reaches the grave, the remains are interred.

sentences.zh: 施銘旌志石於壙內，掩壙復土，乃祠后土於墓。

translations.literal: Place the memorial pennant and epitaph stone inside the chamber, cover the chamber and return the earth, then sacrifice to the Earth Queen at the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial pennant and epitaph stone are placed inside the chamber, the chamber is closed and the earth restored, and the Earth Queen is sacrificed to at the tomb.

sentences.zh: 題主，奉安。

translations.literal: Inscribe the tablet; install it in place.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit tablet is inscribed and installed.

sentences.zh: 升車，反哭。

translations.literal: Mount the carriage; return and wail.
translations.idiomatic: The mourners mount the carriage and return home to wail.

sentences.zh: 凡虞祭，葬之日，日中而虞，柔日再虞，剛日三虞。

translations.literal: For comfort sacrifices: on the burial day, the first comfort sacrifice at midday; the second on a yin day, the third on a yang day.
translations.idiomatic: For comfort sacrifices: on the burial day the first is performed at midday; the second on a yin day, the third on a yang day.

sentences.zh: 若去家經宿以上，則初虞於墓所行之。

translations.literal: If more than one night's journey from home, the first comfort sacrifice is performed at the grave.
translations.idiomatic: If the grave is more than one night's journey from home, the first comfort sacrifice is performed at the burial site.

sentences.zh: 墓遠，途中遇柔日，亦於館所行之。

translations.literal: If the grave is far and a yin day is encountered en route, it is also performed at the lodge.
translations.idiomatic: If the grave is distant and a yin day falls during the journey, the second sacrifice is performed at the lodging along the way.

sentences.zh: 若三虞，必俟至家而後行。

translations.literal: For the third comfort sacrifice, one must wait until reaching home before performing it.
translations.idiomatic: The third comfort sacrifice must wait until the mourners have returned home.

sentences.zh: 三虞後，遇剛日卒哭。

translations.literal: After the three comfort sacrifices, on the next yang day perform the ended wailing.
translations.idiomatic: After the three comfort sacrifices, the ended wailing is performed on the next yang day.

sentences.zh: 明日祔家廟。

translations.literal: The next day install the tablet in the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the tablet is installed in the family temple.

sentences.zh: 期而小祥。

translations.literal: At one year perform the lesser felicitations.
translations.idiomatic: After one year comes the lesser felicitations.

sentences.zh: 喪至此凡十三月，不計閏。

translations.literal: Mourning to this point totals thirteen months, intercalary months not counted.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning to this point totals thirteen months, not counting intercalary months.

sentences.zh: 古卜日祭，今止用初忌，喪主乃易練服。

translations.literal: Anciently one divined the day for sacrifice; now only the first death anniversary is used, and the chief mourner then changes to the training-dress.
translations.idiomatic: Anciently the sacrifice day was divined; now only the first death anniversary is observed, and the chief mourner then changes to the training-dress.

sentences.zh: 再期而大祥。

translations.literal: At two years perform the greater felicitations.
translations.idiomatic: After two years come the greater felicitations.

sentences.zh: 喪至此凡二十五月，亦止用第二忌日祭。

translations.literal: Mourning to this point totals twenty-five months; again only the second death anniversary is used for the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning to this point totals twenty-five months; again only the second death anniversary is observed.

sentences.zh: 陳禫服，告遷於祠堂。

translations.literal: Display the sacrificial dress; announce the transfer to the ancestral hall.
translations.idiomatic: The sacrificial dress is displayed, and the transfer to the ancestral hall is announced.

sentences.zh: 改題神主，遞遷而西，奉神主入於祠堂。

translations.literal: Revise the inscription on the spirit tablet, shift positions westward in succession, and bring the spirit tablet into the ancestral hall.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit tablet is reinscribed, earlier tablets are shifted westward in succession, and the tablet is brought into the ancestral hall.

sentences.zh: 徹靈座，奉遷主埋於墓側。

translations.literal: Remove the spirit seat; bury the transferred tablet beside the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit seat is removed, and the old tablet is buried beside the tomb.

sentences.zh: 大祥後，間一月而禫。

translations.literal: One month after the greater felicitations comes the sacrificial transition.
translations.idiomatic: One month after the greater felicitations comes the sacrificial transition.

sentences.zh: 喪到此計二十有七月。

translations.literal: Mourning to this point counts twenty-seven months.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning to this point totals twenty-seven months.

sentences.zh: 卜日，喪主禫服詣祠堂，祗薦禫事。

translations.literal: On a chosen day, the chief mourner in sacrificial dress goes to the ancestral hall and reverently presents the sacrificial rite.
translations.idiomatic: On a chosen day the chief mourner, wearing sacrificial dress, goes to the ancestral hall and reverently performs the sacrificial rite.

sentences.zh: 其在遠聞喪者，始聞，易服，哭而行。

translations.literal: For those far away who learn of the death: upon first hearing, change clothes, weep, and travel.
translations.idiomatic: For those far from home who learn of a death: upon first hearing, they change clothes, weep, and set out.

sentences.zh: 至家，憑殯哭，四日而成服。

translations.literal: Upon reaching home, weep before the coffin; after four days complete mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching home they weep before the coffin and complete mourning dress after four days.

sentences.zh: 若未得行，則設位，四日而變服。

translations.literal: If unable to travel, set up a mourning seat; after four days change to mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: If they cannot travel, a mourning seat is set up and mourning dress is assumed after four days.

sentences.zh: 若既葬，則先哭諸墓，歸詣靈座前哭，四日成服。

translations.literal: If burial has already taken place, first weep at the tomb, then return and weep before the spirit seat; after four days complete mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: If burial has already taken place, they first weep at the tomb, then return to weep before the spirit seat and complete mourning dress after four days.

sentences.zh: 齊衰以下聞喪，爲位而哭。

translations.literal: For those in qi- and si-grade mourning who hear of the death: set up a seat and weep.
translations.idiomatic: Those in qi- and si-grade mourning who hear of a death set up a mourning seat and weep.

sentences.zh: 若奔喪，則至家成服。

translations.literal: If rushing to the funeral, upon reaching home complete mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: If they rush home for the funeral, they complete mourning dress upon arrival.

sentences.zh: 若不奔喪，四日成服。

translations.literal: If not rushing to the funeral, complete mourning dress after four days.
translations.idiomatic: If they do not rush home, they complete mourning dress after four days.

sentences.zh: 凡有改葬者，孝子以下及妻、妾、女子子，俱緦麻服，周親以下素服。

translations.literal: For reburials, the filial son and below, plus wife, concubines, and daughters all wear the finest hemp; close kin below wear plain white.
translations.idiomatic: For reburials, the filial son and his household—wife, concubines, and daughters—all wear the finest hemp mourning; close kin below them wear plain white.

sentences.zh: 不設祖奠，無反哭，無方相魌頭，餘如常葬之儀。

translations.literal: No ancestral offering at departure, no return wailing, no exorcist or demon mask; otherwise as in regular burial rites.
translations.idiomatic: There is no ancestral offering at departure, no return wailing, and no exorcist or demon mask; otherwise the rites follow the regular burial ceremony.

sentences.zh: 既葬，就吉帷靈座前一虞。

translations.literal: After burial, perform one comfort sacrifice before the auspicious spirit seat within the curtained hall.
translations.idiomatic: After burial, one comfort sacrifice is performed before the spirit seat within the auspicious curtained hall.

sentences.zh: 孝子以下，出就別所，釋緦服素服而還。

translations.literal: The filial son and below withdraw to a separate place, remove the finest hemp and plain dress, and return.
translations.idiomatic: The filial son and his household withdraw to another place, remove their mourning dress, and return.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十六年四月，除期服奔喪之制。

translations.literal: Fourth month, twenty-sixth year of Hongwu, the regulation requiring one-year-mourning relatives to rush to funerals was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Hongwu 26, the rule permitting officials to rush home for one-year mourning was abolished.

sentences.zh: 先是百官聞祖父母、伯叔、兄弟喪，俱得奔赴。

translations.literal: Previously, all officials who heard of grandparents', uncles', and brothers' deaths were permitted to rush home.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, all officials were permitted to rush home upon hearing of a grandparent's, uncle's, or brother's death.

sentences.zh: 至是吏部言：「祖父母、伯叔、兄弟皆系期年服。

translations.literal: At this point the Ministry of Personnel said: "Grandparents, uncles, and brothers all require one-year mourning dress."
translations.idiomatic: At this point the Ministry of Personnel argued: "Grandparents, uncles, and brothers all require one-year mourning."

sentences.zh: 若俱令奔喪守制，或一人連遭五六期喪，或道路數千里，則居官日少，更易繁數，曠官廢事。

translations.literal: If all were required to rush to mourning and observe the full rites, one person might in succession suffer five or six one-year bereavements, or the road might be several thousand li—then days in office would be few, replacements frequent, posts left vacant and affairs neglected.
translations.idiomatic: If every such bereavement required rushing home and full observance, one official might suffer five or six one-year mourning periods in succession, or face journeys of thousands of li—leaving too few days in office, too many replacements, and neglected public business.

sentences.zh: 今後除父母、祖父母承重者丁憂外，其餘期喪不許奔，但遣人致祭。

translations.literal: Henceforth except for parents and grandparents when bearing the chief mourning obligation, other one-year bereavements shall not permit rushing home; only send someone to perform the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, except for parents and grandparents when bearing the chief mourning obligation, officials may not rush home for other one-year bereavements but may send a representative to perform the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The proposal was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: " The court approved.

sentences.zh: ○士庶人喪禮

translations.literal: ○ Mourning rites for gentry and commoners
translations.idiomatic: ○ On mourning rites for gentry and commoners

sentences.zh: 《集禮》及《會典》所載，大略仿品官制，稍有損益。

translations.literal: What is recorded in the 《Collected Rites》 and the 《Institutional Compendium》 largely follows the ranked-official system, with slight additions and reductions.
translations.idiomatic: What the 《Collected Rites》 and the 《Institutional Compendium》 record largely follows the ranked-official system, with slight modifications.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年，御史高元侃言：「京師人民，循習舊俗。

translations.literal: First year of Hongwu, Censor Gao Yuankan said: "The people of the capital follow old customs."
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 1, Censor Gao Yuankan said: "The people of the capital still follow old customs."

sentences.zh: 凡有喪葬，設宴，會親友，作樂娛屍，竟無哀慼之情，甚非所以爲治。

translations.literal: For all funerals they hold banquets, gather kin and friends, make music to entertain the corpse—utterly without grief; this is very far from proper governance.
translations.idiomatic: At every funeral they hold banquets, gather kin and friends, and make music to entertain the corpse, showing no grief at all—hardly the conduct befitting an ordered state.

sentences.zh: 乞禁止以厚風化。

translations.literal: I beg that this be prohibited to improve customs.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that this be prohibited so as to improve public morals.

sentences.zh: 」乃令禮官定民喪服之制。

translations.literal: " Thereupon ritual officials were ordered to fix regulations for commoners' mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: " The throne then ordered ritual officials to fix regulations for commoners' mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 五年詔定：「庶民襲衣一稱，用深衣一、大帶一、履一雙，裙袴衫襪隨所用。

translations.literal: Fifth year imperial decree fixed: "Commoners' burial garments one set: one deep robe, one great girdle, one pair of shoes; skirt, trousers, shirt, and socks as needed."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year an imperial decree fixed: "Commoners' burial garments consist of one set: one deep robe, one great girdle, and one pair of shoes; skirt, trousers, shirt, and socks as needed."

sentences.zh: 飯用粱，含錢三。

translations.literal: Grain placed in the mouth uses fine grain; mouth-offering money three coins.
translations.idiomatic: Fine grain is placed in the mouth, and three coins are included in the mouth-offering.

sentences.zh: 銘旌用紅絹五尺。

translations.literal: Memorial pennant uses five feet of red silk.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial pennant is made of five feet of red silk.

sentences.zh: 斂隨所有，衣衾及親戚禭儀隨所用。

translations.literal: Encoffining uses whatever is available; clothing, quilts, and kin's supplemental garments as needed.
translations.idiomatic: Encoffining uses whatever is available; clothing, quilts, and supplemental garments from kin are added as circumstances allow.

sentences.zh: 棺用堅木，油杉爲上，柏次之，土杉鬆又次之。

translations.literal: Coffin uses hard wood: oil-treated fir best, cypress next, local fir and pine again next.
translations.idiomatic: The coffin is of hard wood: oil-treated fir is best, cypress next, and local fir or pine again next.

sentences.zh: 用黑漆、金漆，不得用硃紅。

translations.literal: Black lacquer and gold lacquer may be used; cinnabar red may not.
translations.idiomatic: Black lacquer and gold lacquer may be used; cinnabar red may not.

sentences.zh: 明器一事。

translations.literal: Burial objects—one type.
translations.idiomatic: Burial objects are limited to one kind.

sentences.zh: 功布以白布三尺引柩。

translations.literal: Merit cloth: white cloth three feet to lead the bier.
translations.idiomatic: Merit cloth consists of three feet of white cloth to lead the bier.

sentences.zh: 柳車以衾覆棺。

translations.literal: Willow cart: quilt covers the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: The willow cart carries the coffin covered by a quilt.

sentences.zh: 志石二片，如官之儀。

translations.literal: Epitaph stones two pieces, as in the official rite.
translations.idiomatic: Two epitaph stones are used, following the official ceremony.

sentences.zh: 塋地圍十八步。

translations.literal: Grave enclosure eighteen paces in circumference.
translations.idiomatic: The grave enclosure measures eighteen paces around.

sentences.zh: 祭用豕，隨家有無。

translations.literal: Sacrifice uses a pig, according to household means.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifices use a pig, according to what the household can afford.

sentences.zh: 」又詔：「古之喪禮，以哀慼爲本，治喪之具，稱家有無。

translations.literal: " Again a decree: "Ancient mourning rites took grief as the foundation; funerary implements should suit household means."
translations.idiomatic: " Another decree stated: "Ancient mourning rites took grief as their foundation, and funerary implements should suit a household's means."

sentences.zh: 近代以來，富者奢僭犯分，力不足者稱貸財物，誇耀殯送，及有惑於風水，停柩經年，不行安葬。

translations.literal: In recent times the wealthy extravagantly usurp rank, while those without means borrow goods to boast at the funeral procession; some, deluded by geomancy, leave the coffin for years without burial.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times the wealthy have grown extravagant and usurped rank; those without means borrow goods to put on a show at the funeral; some, misled by geomancy, leave coffins unburied for years.

sentences.zh: 宜令中書省臣集議定制，頒行遵守，違者論罪。

translations.literal: The Secretariat ministers should gather to fix regulations, promulgate for observance; violators punished by law.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat ministers should gather to fix regulations, promulgate them for observance, and punish violators by law.

sentences.zh: 」又諭禮部曰：「古有掩骼埋胔之令，近世狃元俗，死者或以火焚，而投其骨於水。

translations.literal: " Again instruction to the Ministry of Rites: "Anciently there were orders to gather exposed bones and bury scattered flesh; in recent times people cling to Yuan custom—some burn the dead with fire and cast the bones into water."
translations.idiomatic: " The throne also instructed the Ministry of Rites: "Anciently there were orders to gather exposed bones and bury scattered flesh, but in recent times people cling to Yuan custom—some burn the dead and cast the bones into water."

sentences.zh: 傷恩敗俗，莫此爲甚。

translations.literal: No injury to grace or violation of custom exceeds this.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing does more violence to human feeling or public morals.

sentences.zh: 其禁止之。

translations.literal: Prohibit it.
translations.idiomatic: This is to be prohibited.

sentences.zh: 若貧無地者，所在官司擇寬閒地爲義冢，俾之葬埋。

translations.literal: If poor and without land, the local offices in each place select open ground to make a public burial mound, enabling burial.
translations.idiomatic: Where the poor lacked land for burial, local authorities in each locality were to set aside open ground as a public graveyard so the dead could be interred.

sentences.zh: 或有宦遊遠方不能歸葬者，官給力費以歸之。」

translations.literal: Or if some serving as officials far from home cannot return to bury, the government supplies labor and expenses for their return."
translations.idiomatic: If officials serving far from home could not return to bury their dead, the government was to supply labor and expenses for the journey home."

sentences.zh: ○服紀

translations.literal: ○ Records of Mourning Garments
translations.idiomatic: ○ On mourning garments and periods

sentences.zh: 明初頒《大明令》，凡喪服等差，多因前代之舊。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Ming, the 《Great Ming Statutes》 was promulgated; as for mourning-garment gradations, most followed the old practice of previous ages.
